rows.anchor:

rows.anchor: ## C. The closing sequence
rows.statement: An 11-step dependency-ordered (not importance-ordered) closing sequence is specified: (1) enumerate 𝒪 [HUMAN D-1]; (2) ratify/revise exogenous authority and govern the schema vocabulary [HUMAN D-2]; (3) decide Determination's scope [HUMAN D-3]; (4) derive the congruence and K* for the fixed 𝒪; (5) replace Σ with the ≥5-axis product; (6) split A into A_struct+qualification layer, make ℛ first-class, restore H; (7) type Context, define evidence identity; (8) audit ordinal-arithmetic rules; (9) EKP engineering repairs; (10) run the day-1 selection precision/recall experiment; (11) freeze one corpus tree before the next verification pass.

rows.anchor: An operation o is MANDATORY iff removing o makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law INEXPRESSIBLE ... This is a derivation, not a preference: the laws are corpus text, the forcing relation is entailment
rows.statement: States and applies the derivation principle for operation mandatoriness: an operation is mandatory iff its removal makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law (e.g. 'Remove != Withdraw', 'Determination != Decision') inexpressible; encodes 26 such laws (with repetition-count weights as evidence weight, e.g. 'Expression != Meaning' at 71) and a table of which operation(s) each law forces, e.g. 'Determination != Decision' (weight 19) forces Determine, 'Observation != Evidence' (weight 20) forces Qualify.

rows.anchor: 'Transform', 'Merge', 'Split' are named in 256.2 and forced by NO law. ... 'Qualify' and 'Determine' ARE forced ... but appear in NEITHER 256.2 NOR 259.7. The corpus's own enumeration MISSES two operations its own laws force.
rows.statement: Result: Transform, Merge, Split and Reintroduce are named in the corpus's own registry (s256.2/s259.7) but forced by no non-collapse law (their necessity is asserted, not entailed); conversely Qualify, Determine and Derive are forced by laws with weights 20/19/18 respectively but appear in NEITHER s256.2 nor s259.7 -- so the laws under-determine O in one direction and the corpus's own enumeration over/under-determines it in the other, making set-membership not derivable from the laws alone.

rows.anchor: FALSE AS STATED · TRUE IN SUBSTANCE · AND THE SUBSTANCE IS SHARPER THAN EITHER. ... So the missing premise is not the ENUMERATION. It is the NORMATIVE CLOSURE -- which of the candidates are mandatory.
rows.statement: Tests and refines the claim 'O was never explicitly defined': FALSE as stated (s256.2 enumerates 9 ops in a boxed formula, s259.7 adds Validate/Assess/Promote/Reintroduce/Replay plus a five-class partition) but TRUE in substance (s256.2 itself calls its table 'a reconstruction target, not a claim that all nine are already formally defined', and s259.18 states the ∀T∈T-incompleteness problem as its own boxed negative result, so this was never an independent discovery by any verification track) -- the missing premise is normative closure (which candidates are mandatory), not enumeration.

rows.anchor: non-collapse laws extracted (distinct) : 26 ... operations FORCED : 14 ... Two STRUCTURES are forced as a by-product, and neither is an operation: <D_t> ... <serialize>
rows.statement: Derivation principle (o is mandatory iff removing it makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law inexpressible) applied to 26 distinct measured non-collapse laws: 14 operations forced (Authorize weight 45; Revise/Supersede 41; Promote 26; Qualify 20; Add 19; Determine 19; Derive 18; Replay 12; Assess/Validate 11; Remove/Withdraw/Reject weight 1 each), plus two non-operation structures forced as a by-product: <D_t> (recognised-dimension set, forced by UNKNOWN != ABSENT) and <serialize> (canonical form, forced by Expression != Meaning, the corpus's most-repeated law at 71 occurrences).

rows.anchor: Qualify, Determine, Derive are entailed by laws the corpus repeats 20, 19 and 18 times respectively -- and appear in neither §256.2 nor §259.7. ... Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce. The corpus never writes 'Merge != X', so nothing entails that Merge must exist.
rows.statement: Two-sided mismatch between the derived forced set and the corpus's own named registry: Qualify, Determine, Derive are forced by frequently-repeated laws (20/19/18 occurrences) yet appear in NEITHER s256.2 nor s259.7 (a G5 promotion gap, not a G1 semantic gap); conversely Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce are named in the registry but forced by no non-collapse law (their necessity asserted, not entailed -- Transform's high usage, 8 of 9 kernel phases, is evidence of centrality, not mandatoriness).

rows.statement: O is bounded but not determined: a 14-element lower bound and an 18-element upper bound are both derivable with no human input, along with the five-class partition and congruence rule (independently re-derivable since congruence is a property of an algebra's operations on its carrier, so an operation reading H is not an operation on K); only membership of the 4-operation undetermined band in the mandatory set is not derivable, because 'mandatory' is a normative predicate that no corpus of descriptions can entail -- this is D-1.

rows.anchor: The theory's deficit was never discovery. It was transcription: three successive reductions (ℛ 8→3 fields, status 10→2 values, DC 7→6 components) each discarded something the corpus had established, and each loss was later rediscovered as a fundamental gap.
rows.statement: Final headline argument answering the mandate's central question: KnowledgeOS does NOT need a new theory -- of 34 reconciled gaps, 8 are promotions (two running/passing code), 6 are repairs of execution-falsified formulations, 5 are refinements, 4 are normative choices, exactly 1 requires innovation; the recurring failure pattern is three successive transcription reductions (relation 8-to-3 fields, status 10-to-2 values, a 7-to-6-component DC reduction), each of which discarded corpus-established content that was later independently rediscovered as a 'fundamental' gap.

rows.anchor: What remains open — and it is only this: are Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce mandatory or optional? ... What this decision does NOT block: K is invariant across all 16 subsets.
rows.statement: D-1 narrowed: only whether Transform/Merge/Split/Reintroduce are mandatory or optional remains open (a normative predicate no corpus of descriptions entails), narrowed from the apparently-foundational 'what is O' question; explicitly does not block K's construction (band-invariant), only the congruence proof and T-relative minimality; four options offered (a) all four mandatory, (b) none, (c) Transform only, (d) open-ended-with-mandatory-core, with (c)/(d) recommended.

rows.anchor: This is not a derivation. It is a RESTATEMENT: the register was written by reading an operation off each distinction, so the necessity test over it is a TAUTOLOGY. It cannot eliminate a single member, and it cannot discover a member the register's author did not already name.
rows.statement: Executing the map distinction->required-operation over step 272A's 19-row D_mandatory register shows it is total and injective (a bijection): every operation is the unique realizer of exactly one distinction. Applying the stated necessity criterion (o in O_core iff exists d in D_mandatory: Remove(o) implies Loss(d)) over this register therefore returns 'all 19 necessary' by construction -- a tautological restatement of how the register was authored, not an independent derivation, and it can neither eliminate nor discover any member.

assumptions.statement: The 19-row D_mandatory register is a faithful transcription of step 272A §272A.17

lineage_claims.quote: the necessity test over it is a TAUTOLOGY

experiment.hypothesis: The corpus's own necessity criterion over D_mandatory can discriminate necessary from unnecessary operations.
experiment.setup: Transcribe the 19-row (distinction, required operation) register from step 272A verbatim.
experiment.assumptions: transcription fidelity to §272A.17
experiment.method: Compute whether the map distinction->operation is total and injective; compute duplicate/multi-realizer counts.
experiment.result: Map is total and injective (bijection); |O_core|=19=|O_sem|, all rows 'necessary' by construction.
experiment.interpretation: The criterion is a tautology over this register and cannot discriminate.
experiment.limitations: Only tests the D_mandatory form of the criterion, not R_mandatory since that set is never enumerated.
experiment.conclusion: The necessity criterion is only informative over a requirement set derived independently of the operation vocabulary; the commission should derive R_A from ratified invariants and flow instead of any candidate list.

rows.anchor: A6 ADVERSARIAL: can evidence volume ever commit? ... state: 1 Accepted item, {len(big_ev)} independent supporting evidence units, NO authority act
rows.statement: An adversarial test constructs a state with one Accepted item backed by 40+ independent supporting evidence units and no authority act, then runs every pooled operation against it to see whether any produces a Committed item -- testing whether evidence volume alone can cross the A6 authority boundary.

experiment.hypothesis: Evidence volume alone (without an authority act) can never cross the A6 Accepted->Committed boundary.
experiment.setup: K state with 1 Accepted proposition item backed by >=40 independent supporting evidence units, no authority act recorded.
experiment.assumptions: the operation pool and probe functions correctly model candidate operations
experiment.inputs: the heavy evidentiary state, every operation in POOL and PROBES, every argument in ALLARGS
experiment.method: apply every operation to the heavy state for every argument; check whether any resulting item is committed
experiment.result: script computes and prints count of operations that produced Committed and prints 'A6 HOLDS' if zero
experiment.interpretation: if zero, A6 is confirmed robust against evidence-volume attacks under the modeled operation pool
experiment.limitations: limited to the operations in POOL/PROBES, not the full universe
experiment.conclusion: reported as an executed check; exact printed pass/fail not captured in this source file (see OUT-consistency.txt for the executed result)

rows.anchor: Closure(𝒯) is instantiated as bounded reachability under finite composition ... This is what makes the test executable without resolving the state-equality question that blocks the contracts: reachability needs only a decidable state comparison for deduplication, not a canonical one.
rows.statement: Closure(T) in the necessity criterion is operationalized as bounded reachability under finite composition: a mandatory capability r=(seed,goal) is in Closure(S) iff some finite sequence of operations from S, of length <= the capability's depth bound, carries the seed state to a state satisfying goal. This sidesteps the state-identity/equality gap that blocks the per-operation contracts, because reachability search only needs a decidable comparison for deduplication, not a canonical equality relation.

rows.statement: Mechanical effect-equivalence testing over the 55-name candidate pool found 39 distinct effect classes: 12 candidate names (Compare/Equal/Evaluate/Explain/ExplainRevision/Identity/LineageQuery/ProvenanceQuery/Query/SupersessionHistory, plus Trace and noop) are pure reads that never change state on any probe and are excluded from the minimality search entirely; seven further groups of corpus names collapse under the ratified guards to a single effect each (Add=Assert=Create, Accept=Determine, ChangePolicy=EnactPolicyVersion, LinkEvidence=Support, Promote=Transform, Remove=Retract). This independently re-derives, by execution, step 259 §259.8's argued rule that only state-transforming operations enter the primary congruence test.

The explicit corollary: corroboration across the research record (how many sources mention an operation) is not the same as necessity against the ratified surface -- this is not a recommendation to drop the corroborated names, but a statement that the ratified surface does not quantify over them, so their inclusion needs a different justification than ratified entailment.

rows.statement: Eight structural disagreements (D1-D10, D8 flagged as 'the largest gap') are catalogued among the corpus's operation enumerations: LinkEvidence exists in 277 but not 272A (D1); Split is core in 277, absent (not rejected) from 272A (D2); Infer is core in 272A but absent from 277 / UNRESOLVED in 250 (D3); Replay has three incompatible positions across sources (D4); Trace/Query/Compare/Identity/Equal are REQUIRED in 272A but merely 'Supporting'/excluded in 277 (D5); DetectContradiction/Resolve/Identity/Equal/Assess appear in the later 272A but are wholly absent from 277's inventory despite never being reconciled (D6); Authorize/Validate are both inside and 'REQUIRED EXTERNAL' within 272A itself, an internal inconsistency (D7); representation ops are excluded by 272A/277 and included by 276 (D10); and most significantly (D8) Transform/Add/Revise, which 249/250 mark as CORPUS-ESTABLISHED state operations, vanish entirely from the later 272A and 277 kernels (replaced by Assert) with no document ever stating that Assert supersedes Add or that Transform was demoted.

rows.anchor: step 257 §257.37 states it in the corpus's own voice: 'We still cannot formally decide K=? because Identity is not fully specified, Equality is not specified, EpistemicStatus is not frozen… Therefore the correct next move is not to select a kernel.'
rows.statement: Of the commission's three C-5 prerequisites, all three are DEFERRED at the contracts level: a closed invariant register (canon asserts I-1..I-12/FA-1 additions but never asserts these are ALL of them; step 232 §232.39 independently proposes a different, unproven five-invariant minimal candidate register); typed rejection semantics (the corpus's one existing typed-rejection proposal, from TRANSFORMATION-CANONICAL-MODEL.md §1, has only three kinds and is shown insufficient against step 232's evidence-admissibility condition and I-12 legality, so a five-kind vocabulary was supplied instead, NORMATIVE DECISION REQUIRED); and a state identity/equality rule (absent from the entire corpus, with step 257 §257.37 stating in its own voice that K=? cannot be formally decided and that 'the correct next move is not to select a kernel'). However, the executed minimality TEST (task 3) was not blocked by any of the three, since reachability only needs a decidable (not canonical) state comparison -- only the per-operation CONTRACTS (task 7) are blocked by them.
missing: closed invariant register
typed rejection vocabulary (ratified)
state identity/equality rule (ratified)

rows.anchor: Three fields cannot be canonically filled for ANY operation FORMALLY SHOWN ... invariant obligations ... failure semantics ... postconditions (partly)
rows.statement: Three of the commission's eleven contract fields cannot be canonically filled for ANY of the 23 contracted operations, each for a structural reason: 'invariant obligations' because the invariant register is not closed (canon never asserts I-1..I-12+FA-1 are ALL invariants; a competing five-element register exists at step 232 §232.39); 'failure semantics' because canon defines no rejection vocabulary at all (the corpus's only typed-rejection proposal has 3 kinds, insufficient for I-12 legality or step 232's evidence-admissibility refusal); 'postconditions' partly, because state equality is undefined corpus-wide (step 257 §257.37) so any postcondition of the form K'=f(K) is undecidable and must be restated as field-level assertions instead.

rows.anchor: 23 operation blocks covering 24 operations ... 253 commission cells ... RATIFIED-SOURCED 27 ... EXECUTED 24 ... PROPOSED 12 ... NORMATIVE DECISION REQUIRED 69 ... no operation has a complete canonical contract, and none can have one until P-8/P-9/P-10 of MINIMALITY-RESULT.md §5.3 are settled.
rows.statement: A mechanically-verified contract-completion scorecard over 23 blocks (276 rows, 253 commission cells, no blank cells): 27 cells RATIFIED-SOURCED, 24 EXECUTED, 12 PROPOSED, 69 marked NORMATIVE-DECISION-REQUIRED (46 of which are the two universally-open fields, invariant obligations and failure semantics; the rest are operation-specific). Compared against the governed baseline (OPERATION-CONTRACT-GAP.md §B: 2 cells fully fixed, 9 partial, 88 empty across 9 capabilities), this represents substantial new grounding, but the honest overall verdict stated is that no operation has a complete canonical contract, and none can until three named prior canonical decisions (P-8 state equality, P-9 closed invariant register, P-10 typed rejection vocabulary) are settled.

rows.anchor: another declares it UNCONSTRUCTED: 'the same five states fall into 2, 3, 5 or 5 equivalence classes… K₁ = K₂ has no truth value in the theory as it stands,' and 'a relation defined by ∀T ∈ 𝒯 where 𝒯 has no extension is not yet a relation.' ... this is the deepest of the three, and it is circular with the registry
rows.statement: State equality is documented as having two flatly contradictory corpus positions: one lane declares it CLOSED with five defined notions (object, structural, semantic, observational, history, ordered history subset structural subset semantic); another declares it UNCONSTRUCTED, stating the same five example states fall into 2, 3, 5, or 5 equivalence classes depending on which notion is used, that 'K1=K2 has no truth value in the theory as it stands', and that a relation quantified over an operation set with no fixed extension 'is not yet a relation'. A further circularity is named: an equality quantified over the operation set T needs T fixed; but T's contracts have postconditions that need equality -- the deepest of the three C-5 prerequisites, resolved for the executed minimality test only by substituting decidable reachability for canonical equality (MINIMALITY-RESULT.md §6), not resolved for the contracts.
missing: which state equality notion is canonical
proof that it is a congruence for the registry's operations

rows.anchor: '⚠ NDR: is the grade STORED in K or RECOMPUTED ON READ?' TRANSFORMATION-CANONICAL-MODEL §2 says recomputed ... step 232 §232.9 stores it ... The two positions are incompatible and both are in the corpus. ... which contradicts KNOWLEDGE-STATE-ALGEBRA §3's 'validate and assess are the only two operations that do not change K'
rows.statement: The Assess contract (C-07) surfaces two distinct corpus contradictions: (1) Assess as contracted here writes the computed grade into K's item field, contradicting KNOWLEDGE-STATE-ALGEBRA.md §3's claim that 'validate and assess are the only two operations that do not change K'; (2) whether the epistemic grade is stored in K or recomputed on read is answered incompatibly by two sources (TRANSFORMATION-CANONICAL-MODEL.md §2: recomputed on read; step 232 §232.9: stored as a component sigma of the state 𝔎). Both are reported as unreconciled NORMATIVE-DECISION-REQUIRED items rather than resolved.

rows.anchor: handoff/02: 'LinkEvidence would MUTATE an assertion, contradicting ReplayAssertion's immutability invariant. Unreconciled.' ⚠ NDR — T-3 reconciliation, named not made. Three routes: (a) ... (b) ... (c) evidence links live in ℛ, not in the assertion ... Route (c) is the only one that satisfies both sources, and choosing it is still a normative act
rows.statement: For the commission's T-3 reconciliation task on LinkEvidence (recorded UNRECONCILED because it mutates an assertion, contradicting the executed algebra's ReplayAssertion immutability invariant), three non-interchangeable repair routes are named: (a) evidence is fixed at assertion creation, so new evidence produces a new assertion plus a relation (the executed algebra's position); (b) evidence is a mutable field, so the immutability invariant is amended instead; (c) evidence links live in the relation set R, not in the assertion, so nothing is mutated (277 §277.14's proposal). Route (c) is identified as the only one satisfying both sources simultaneously, but choosing it is still flagged as a normative act, and it would remove LinkEvidence from the state operations entirely, changing capability A5's witness and the necessary-operation core computed in MINIMALITY-RESULT.md.

rows.anchor: '⚠ NDR: replaying an action re-executes it in the world.' This is the sharpest safety question in the registry, and no corpus document addresses it ... replay reproduces the state ... is an equation between states, and state equality is undefined
rows.statement: The Act contract (C-19) names what it calls 'the sharpest safety question in the registry': replaying an authorized Act operation would re-execute its real-world side effect (not merely recompute a state), and no corpus document addresses whether replay of action operations is even safe or meaningful, distinct from replay of pure state-transition operations. Compounding this, Replay's own postcondition ('replay reproduces the state') is an equation between states that is undecidable pending the unresolved state-equality question (§1.3/C-5), and Replay's determinism is shown EXECUTED to be order-dependent, traced specifically to Relate's acyclicity guard (the same edge can be admissible in one insertion order and rejected as a cycle in another) -- identified as the corpus's source of replay's order-dependence.
missing: safety semantics for replaying real-world-effecting operations
a canonical operation-pair commutation table for replay determinism

rows.anchor: 'supports' is NOT transitive — 'evidential support cannot be propagated along chains; any implementation that does so is unsound'; 'contradicts' is a TOLERANCE relation, never an equivalence — 'there are no contradiction classes'
rows.statement: Two algebraic warnings are recorded for the relation-constructing operations (C-23, Relate/Refute): the 'supports' relation is explicitly non-transitive -- evidential support must not be propagated along chains, and any implementation that does so is unsound; and 'contradicts' is a tolerance relation (symmetric, non-transitive by design), never an equivalence relation, so there are no well-defined 'contradiction classes' to partition items into. Additionally, acyclicity of the supersedes/refines/derived_from relation families is stated to be an invariant of the state K, not an optional runtime check.

rows.anchor: I would preserve these four statements separately: Does a minimal operation registry exist under the tested criterion? YES ... Is the minimal registry unique? NO — six found ... Can we select one as canonical from current evidence? NO ... Is the operation registry ratified? NO
rows.statement: The reviewer proposes preserving four separate questions with distinct answers as a governance discipline (a 'healthy outcome'): does a minimal operation registry exist under the tested reachability criterion (YES), is it unique (NO -- six found), can one be selected as canonical from current evidence (NO), is the operation registry ratified (NO). Relatedly, 'minimal under the chosen computational criterion' and 'minimal canonical operation set of KnowledgeOS' are proposed as a permanent terminological distinction for the book and governance record -- the first has been demonstrated non-unique, the second has not been demonstrated at all.

rows.anchor: Do not ask it to resolve the six registries. Do not ask it to choose Reject. Do not ask it to repair I-12 or Art. 8. Do not ask it to write the implementation specification. Let the independent verifier attack the derivation exactly as commissioned.
rows.statement: Explicit governance instruction to quarantine the deriving lane from premature closure of its own open findings: the deriving agent must not be asked to resolve the six registries, choose Reject's typing, repair I-12/Art.8, or write the implementation specification; instead the independent verifier commissioned under C-8/GN-82 must attack the derivation adversarially across six points (AC-1 completeness of the candidate universe, AC-2 an actual entailment chain per necessary operation rather than 'the theory needs it', AC-3 the claimed absence of hidden Sigma/Q_t dependence, AC-4 independent reproduction of the six-registry minimality result including seventh-registry/smaller-registry/miscounted-equivalence checks, AC-5 independent reproduction of the reported I-12/Art.8/A6/Reject/I-11/I-5/I-6 findings, AC-6 entailment provenance for every one of the 15 mandatory capabilities, singled out as 'probably the most important gate'). The proposed sequence is: Derivation -> independent falsification -> reconcile findings -> HPA decision on prerequisite canonical questions -> derive/ratify operation registry -> define transformation semantics -> implementation specification -> implementation/tests.

rows.anchor: If Reject is required to reach the ratified REJECTED state, but its current specification violates I-12 and Art. 8, then there is an internal tension in the ratified architecture. This should become its own architecture/governance issue, rather than being silently solved while defining operations.
rows.statement: The reviewer argues the Reject finding should be escalated to its own independent architecture/governance issue rather than resolved implicitly as a side effect of the operation-registry work, because it reveals a genuine internal tension within the ratified architecture itself (a ratified capability, A8/reach-REJECTED, whose only realizing operation violates two other ratified constraints), not merely a gap in the candidate operation set.

rows.anchor: Book verdict: 8 GREEN · 5 AMBER · 3 RED. No RED may be written around; each requires a decision outside the book lane. ... Part V · V.5 operations | 🔴 RED | IMPLEMENTATION BLOCKER — CANONICAL SEMANTICS NOT ESTABLISHED
rows.statement: A book-production GREEN/AMBER/RED readiness matrix is recorded for every part/chapter of the planned KnowledgeOS book: 8 chapters GREEN (Part I discovery chapters except I.3; Part II reconstruction, frozen/ACCEPTED; Part III architecture, gate-passed; V.1 method; V.3 state; V.4 invariants; Part VI implications), 5 AMBER (Part IV formal programme, admissible only as non-canonical programme history; V.2 objects/identity; V.7 evidence; V.8 governance/authority with GC-1 visible; V.9 software/tests), and 3 RED (I.3 the Lens Programme, gated on a separate 38-document kernel commission BA-ED2-09; V.5 operations and V.6 transformations, both IMPLEMENTATION BLOCKER -- CANONICAL SEMANTICS NOT ESTABLISHED). The rule stated is that no RED chapter may be 'written around' -- each requires a decision outside the book-production lane.

rows.anchor: V.5 and V.6 are now writable as status and dependency — what the blocker is, its evidence, its owner, the prerequisite canonical questions, and the four-statement distinction (exists YES · unique NO · selectable NO · ratified NO) — but not as a canonical operation/transition contract.
rows.statement: Following GN-84 (the derivation's recommended verdict D pending independent falsification), the book-production chapters V.5/V.6 are re-graded from fully blocked to writable-as-status-and-dependency only: they may describe what the blocker is, its evidence, its owner, and the named prerequisite canonical questions, plus the four-statement existence/uniqueness/selectability/ratification distinction -- but may not present any canonical operation or transition contract. rows.path: docs/knowledgeos/reviews/synthesis/prompts/Confirmed first, since you flagged it: t
rows.anchor: First perform a strict three-way comparison: 1. Derivation claim ... 2. Independent falsification result ... 3. Canonical consequence ... RATIFIED → FORMALLY DERIVED → COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED → PROPOSED → OPEN and, crucially, what authority would be required to move it upward?
rows.statement: A proposed reconciliation methodology for when the independent falsification report arrives: perform a strict three-way comparison per claim -- (1) what exactly the derivation established, (2) which claims the independent falsification confirmed, falsified, or could not test, (3) the canonical consequence, classifying each surviving claim on a five-rung epistemic-status ladder (RATIFIED -> FORMALLY DERIVED -> COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED -> PROPOSED -> OPEN) and identifying what authority would be needed to move it up a rung. A fully successful verification outcome is explicitly allowed to be 'the computational result is correct, but it does not establish canon.' An eight-question decision table (registries reproducible? genuinely non-equivalent? smaller registry exists? capabilities actually entailed? Sigma/Q_t genuinely irrelevant? Reject compatible with canon? A6 crossing genuine? unique canonical registry established?) determines the next HPA decision among three paths (resolve prerequisites and rerun; ratify a uniquely established registry; record the algebra as an open architectural decision) -- with a fourth path, 'the six candidates are good enough, choose the most sensible one,' explicitly named and rejected as undoing the established discipline.

rows.anchor: AC-1 · Completeness of the candidate universe — FAIL ... At least twelve enumeration sources are absent from the 17-source list ... at least one live, governance-escalated operation name (unask) is absent from all 57.
rows.statement: Independent primary-source verification finds the derivation's claimed 'complete candidate operation universe' (57 live names, 105 grand union) is materially incomplete: (a) an uncited Question-15 document contains a 24-operation typed-signature taxonomy of which ~19 names appear in neither the live nor historical union, and the derivation's own supporting corpus documents this taxonomy's existence; (b) 'unask' is a live operation name under an open, named normative decision (ND-282-1, GD-08 'No unask' recommended but explicitly 'Recommendation != Decision') absent from both lists; (c) the stated reading ceiling (step 281) is wrong by three steps -- steps 282, 283, 284 exist and unask/Q_t operations live above the ceiling, making the claim 'Q_t appears in none of steps 249/250/256/257/259/272A/277' true only of those seven steps and misleading about the corpus as a whole; (d) steps 260/261 enumerate operations bearing directly on minimality (including 'Deduplicate' as a first-class NORMATIVE/DOMAIN-DEPENDENT row) and are uncited. The reviewer explicitly notes this incompleteness is not epistemically inert: missed names are plausible alternative realizers of capabilities whose core membership rests on unique-writer arguments, so by the derivation's own bias analysis the computed necessary core of 12 and undetermined band of 9 cannot be relied upon as computed values.

lineage_claims.quote: the universe is materially incomplete

rows.anchor: IR-F-1 · RED · The headline obstruction rests on an encoding more permissive than its cited source. ... There is no 'specification' to violate. 256.11 offers a possible semantics, self-marked provisional. ... The encoding is strictly more permissive than the source. op_Reject drops the Proposed restriction entirely.
rows.statement: The derivation's decisive claim (that all six computed minimal registries are inconsistent because Reject's specification violates I-12/Art.8) is refuted as stated: step 256.11's rule is introduced as 'Possible semantics', not a specification, is self-graded provisional (yellow, mostly '?'), and it DOES name a source-status guard (Status(x): Proposed -> Rejected) -- contradicting the derivation's own claim that Reject 'carries no guard on the source status'. The model's op_Reject implementation drops the Proposed restriction entirely, making the Conflicted->Rejected transition a product of the model's encoding, not something licensed by the corpus. Furthermore 'Proposed' is not even a ratified status (the ratified ladder is Candidate<Supported<Accepted), so mapping 256.11's Proposed onto ratified vocabulary is itself an unmade normative choice the derivation never notes. The corrected, weaker finding: Reject's guard is unspecified, so the consistency of every candidate registry is undetermined -- not proven inconsistent.

lineage_claims.quote: The obstruction as stated -- all six registries are inconsistent -- does not survive.

rows.anchor: IR-F-2 · RED · op_Replay does not replay, and the deliverable applies to the record a standard its own code fails. ... It sets a marker. It never folds history back to state.
rows.statement: op_Replay in rm.py only sets a boolean marker (ok = len(k.hist) > 0) and never actually folds history back to state; A15's goal predicate tests exactly that marker, making 'Replay is necessary for A15' a tautology over a field invented for one no-op operation -- yet it is listed among necessities graded FORMALLY SHOWN. This is exactly the same defect (a test that would pass identically whether or not the underlying law were true) that the derivation itself uses to discredit the corpus's withdrawn A6 witness, so the deliverable fails a standard it applies to others. Mitigated by A15 being graded PROPOSED and excluded from two of three registry variants.

rows.anchor: IR-F-3 · RED · 'All minimal sufficient registries, enumerated exactly — six in every variant' is exhaustive for one variant of three. ... A13's witness family is a single hand-constructed size-7 set, self-labelled not proven-minimal.
rows.statement: The claim that 'six minimal registries, enumerated exactly' holds in every variant is true only for R_A_strict (12 capabilities, A13 excluded); for R_A (15) and R_A_ratified (13), A13's witness family is a single hand-constructed, explicitly not-proven-minimal size-7 set substituted for exhaustive enumeration -- so 'six registries' for those two variants is conditional on that one witness, not exhaustive. If A13's true minimal witnesses are size 5-6, both the registry count and minimum size change for those variants. Consequently the 'band invariant at nine across all three sets' (offered as the answer to the AC-6 watch item) follows substantially from mechanically adding one fixed set to every registry rather than being independent evidence of robustness -- much weaker than presented, though the caveat is disclosed in one section (T-3) without being propagated to the headline claims.
missing: A13's true minimal witness family at sizes 5-6

rows.anchor: IR-F-4 · RED · The 'I-12 bypass' is mischaracterised ... It is not a bypass of I-12's prohibition. ... Supported's immediate predecessor is Candidate. ... No rung is skipped ... rm.py:371 Resolve returns to Supported unconditionally, regardless of the pre-suspension rung.
rows.statement: The derivation's 'I-12 bypass' structural discovery is refuted as characterised: I-12 prohibits skipping a rung, but Candidate->Conflicted->Supported reaches Supported from its actual immediate predecessor Candidate, so no rung is skipped and I-12's prohibition is never engaged. The path exists only because rm.py's op_Resolve hardcodes an unconditional return to Supported regardless of the pre-suspension rung -- an undeclared modelling choice (absent from the §0.4 declared-commitments list) that the derivation itself concedes (in §5.3) would change the registry family from six to five if chosen differently. The genuinely dangerous path that WOULD skip a rung, Candidate->Conflicted->Accepted, is never tested, though one of the derivation's own four candidate answers to the resolution-return-rung question would permit it. What survives: the ratified text genuinely never states which rung a governed resolution returns to, so the underlying open question (P-2) is legitimate -- only the 'bypass'/'discovered by execution against the ratified model' framing is refuted.

lineage_claims.quote: the characterisation as 'a finding against the ratified layered state model, discovered by execution' is not [warranted]

rows.anchor: IR-F-5 · RED · A ratified constraint bearing directly on P-2 was never consulted. Constitution Article 8.3: 'Resolution SHALL be forward-only: the conflict record SHALL survive resolution.' The string 'forward-only' occurs zero times in all three deliverables and all five scripts
rows.statement: Constitution Article 8.3 ('Resolution SHALL be forward-only: the conflict record SHALL survive resolution') bears directly on P-2 (which rung a governed CONFLICTED resolution returns to) but is never consulted anywhere across all three deliverables and all five scripts, despite Art.8 being cited roughly twenty times in its §1 sense only. Under either reading of 'forward-only', at least one of the derivation's own four candidate answers to P-2 ('return to the rung held before suspension') is in tension with it. Also unconsulted: Art.8.2 ('Challenge SHALL NOT destroy identity').

rows.anchor: All 13 trace to a genuine ratified or authorized anchor. None fails on 'the theory needs it.' ... A13's separation of a ratified capability from a PROPOSED formulation is exemplary discipline.
rows.statement: The reviewer independently traced each of the 13 claimed RATIFIED-FORCED capabilities (A1-A13, excluding the two PROPOSED A14/A15) individually against primary ratified/authorized text (v0.1, v0.2, FA-1, the Constitution) rather than the derivation's own citation column, and confirmed all 13 SURVIVE (trace to a genuine anchor, none manufactured on 'the theory needs it'), though two citations are imprecise: A7's cited anchor (SourceObs != SemanticObs) does not itself force an observation->evidence transition (it actually survives via a different, uncited flow-arrow criterion), and A11's phrasing imports the unratified vocabulary term 'dimension' though its underlying UNKNOWN != ABSENT != FALSE content is genuinely ratified.

rows.anchor: The correct ground is underdetermination, not inconsistency: The six computed registries are neither consistent nor inconsistent with the ratified surface, because the guard on the one operation all six must contain ... is not specified anywhere ... P-11 recorded as prior to P-1…P-10 ... what is the operation universe, and what act closes it?
rows.statement: The reviewer agrees with the derivation's recommended terminal verdict D but on a different, weaker, and more defensible ground: not that the six registries are proven INCONSISTENT with the ratified surface (refuted per IR-F-1), but that they are UNDERDETERMINED -- neither consistent nor inconsistent -- because Reject's guard is unspecified rather than violated. D is further over-determined by P-8/P-9/P-10 (independently reconfirmed: no state equality, no closed invariant register, no rejection vocabulary), P-1 and P-2 (surviving on corrected grounds), P-3 through P-7 (each a real documented disagreement), and critically a new eleventh decision P-11 -- 'what is the operation universe, and what act closes it?' -- introduced by AC-1's FAIL and explicitly recorded as PRIOR to all of P-1 through P-10, since the operation universe itself, not merely its membership criteria, is shown incomplete. The reviewer also separately argues verdict B is not supportable (non-exhaustive for two of three variants, and conditional on two now-corrected modelling choices) and verdict C would be defensible but under-reports what the test achieved.

lineage_claims.quote: D still follows. But the record should carry the weaker, accurate ground

rows.anchor: All five scripts re-run to byte-identical output under an independent Python 3.13.2 (only the wall-clock line differs). Rare and creditable. ... The circularity/bijection finding is correct and important. ... The step 025a-2 §36 Commit result is correct and correctly scoped ... The strongest single result in the deliverable.
rows.statement: Nine GREEN findings confirm the derivation's genuine strengths: byte-identical independent reproduction of all five scripts (IR-F-17); the closure computation is genuine bounded BFS with no law-lookup table, clearing the bar the derivation itself sets for oderive.py (IR-F-18); the oderive.py methodological accusation is accurate and fairly stated line-by-line (IR-F-19); the 272A D_mandatory bijection/circularity finding is correct and is the load-bearing methodological move justifying deriving the requirement set independently (IR-F-20); all 13 RATIFIED-FORCED anchors trace to primary text (IR-F-21); I-5/I-6/I-9/I-2/Art.7/A6-for-the-pool invariant results all check out (IR-F-22); the step 025a-2 §36 Commit-crosses-A6 result is 'the strongest single result in the deliverable' (IR-F-23); the failure-semantics blockage is real, not a framing artifact (IR-F-24); and multiplicity (the six registries) is genuinely reported, not resolved, with no registry privileged in the prose (IR-F-25).

Question 2 shows the six are not established as distinct and question 3 shows a smaller set is not excluded, so plausibility-selection would choose among sets whose distinctness is itself unproven.
rows.statement: Of four possible dispositions after the two-lane review, three are permitted (A: resolve prerequisite canonical decisions -- at minimum P-11 universe closure and P-1 Reject typing, re-examine the return rung against Art.8.3, fix op_Replay, close registry-enumeration variants 2-3, then rerun the derivation -- assessed as 'the only move the evidence supports'; B: ratify a uniquely established registry -- unavailable since question 8 answers NO; C: record the operation algebra as an open architectural decision -- available but discards Task 2's surviving result) and a fourth ('the six candidates are good enough, choose the most sensible one') is explicitly named and FORBIDDEN by GN-85, refused by reference, because the six registries are not established as genuinely distinct (question 2) and a smaller registry is not excluded (question 3) -- so plausibility-selection would choose among sets whose very distinctness is unproven.

rows.anchor: DERIVED ≠ VERIFIED ≠ AUTHORIZED ≠ RATIFIED ≠ CANONICAL ... never transform: 'a minimal registry exists under the tested computational criterion' into: 'KnowledgeOS has a canonical minimal operation set.'
rows.statement: A five-term epistemic status ladder is established as the governing separation for the independent falsification mandate: DERIVED != VERIFIED != AUTHORIZED != RATIFIED != CANONICAL, with the explicit worked example that 'a minimal registry exists under the tested computational criterion' must never be silently transformed into 'KnowledgeOS has a canonical minimal operation set'. A four-statement status table (registry exists under tested criterion: YES per derivation; unique: NO, six found; selectable now: NO; ratified: NO) is fixed as the object the reviewer must independently re-test, explicitly forbidding collapsing the four statements into one.

rows.anchor: Attack A — smaller registry ... Attack B — different decomposition ... Attack C — different primitive boundary ... Attack D — hidden derived operation ... Attack E — hidden state dependency ... Attack F — hidden evidence dependency ... Attack G — replay ... Attack H — rejection ... Attack I — authority boundary ... Attack J — invariant compatibility
rows.statement: A ten-item adversarial attack taxonomy (AC-5) is specified for testing any derived operation registry: (A) can fewer operations satisfy all mandatory capabilities; (B) can one operation be replaced by a sequence of others; (C) are two proposed primitives actually one composite capability; (D) is an alleged operation merely a derived state transition; (E) does an operation only appear necessary because a state distinction was omitted; (F) does an operation require an unratified evidence distinction; (G) can the algebra replay the same history deterministically; (H) do rejection/failure semantics require unratified assumptions; (I) does any operation cross the A6 authority boundary without an authority act; (J) does every operation preserve all applicable ratified invariants.

rows.anchor: Pay particular attention to the historical failure mode already identified in this programme: later constructions being projected backward as though they were earlier canonical requirements. Any such projection must be explicitly flagged.
rows.statement: AC-6 entailment scrutiny requires every claimed mandatory operation/capability to be expressed as CLAIM -> SUPPORTING PREMISE -> EXACT SOURCE -> LOGICAL CONSEQUENCE, with anything not demonstrable classified NOT ENTAILED rather than upgraded from 'plausible'/'consistent with'/'suggested by'/'common practice'. A named recurring corpus failure mode is flagged for special scrutiny: later theoretical constructions being retroactively projected backward as though they were always earlier canonical requirements.

rows.anchor: DERIVE → FALSIFY → DECIDE → RATIFY → DEFINE TRANSFORMATIONS → IMPLEMENT → TEST. Do not skip a stage. ... The most important thing now is to prevent the project from quietly turning 'computationally minimal candidate' into 'KnowledgeOS canonical operation set.'
rows.statement: A seven-stage pipeline discipline is fixed for the operation-registry programme: DERIVE -> FALSIFY -> DECIDE -> RATIFY -> DEFINE TRANSFORMATIONS -> IMPLEMENT -> TEST, with an explicit instruction not to skip a stage. Nine mandatory stop conditions are listed (a ratified artifact would need modification; a governance decision would need inventing; AF-F-31 must be resolved; A6 must be reinterpreted; an unratified construct is required as a premise; a candidate must be selected by preference; a mathematical claim cannot be independently reproduced; the acceptance criteria are insufficient; the invariant register is not closed enough to evaluate operations; rejection semantics are undefined in a way that makes the test undecidable) at which the reviewer must stop and report rather than solve editorially. Four possible outcome scenarios (A: one unique registry survives; B: several genuinely minimal registries survive, a choice-boundary requiring explicit HPA decision; C: minimality itself fails; D: the test is blocked by Reject/A6/invariant semantics, requiring prior architectural decisions) are named as the anticipated space of results.

rows.anchor: AC-1 FAILED. The HPA's own gate reads: 'If any fails, the operation registry is NOT VERIFIED.' ### THE OPERATION REGISTRY IS NOT VERIFIED. ... 'VERIFIED NON-UNIQUENESS' is not available either ... Non-uniqueness is REPORTED, not VERIFIED. ... No second falsification pass can change this determination.
rows.statement: Applying the HPA's own pre-fixed acceptance gate (all of AC-1..AC-6 must PASS, else the registry is NOT VERIFIED) mechanically to the completed evidence: since AC-1 (completeness) FAILED, the operation registry is formally THE OPERATION REGISTRY IS NOT VERIFIED, and the alternate softer outcome 'VERIFIED NON-UNIQUENESS' is also unavailable since it likewise requires all six gates to pass -- so the accurate characterization is that non-uniqueness (six minimal registries) is REPORTED, not VERIFIED. Because completeness is a property of the candidate universe rather than of the testing methodology, no further falsification pass over the same universe can change this determination; only a corrected Task 1 (candidate-universe re-inventory) can.

rows.anchor: | 9 | Rejection semantics | NOT TESTABLE | Canon defines no rejection type or failure vocabulary; failure semantics is blocked for every operation in the contracts. The dimension cannot be evaluated, not merely unevaluated.
rows.statement: The ten-dimension verdict uses a distinct verdict value NOT TESTABLE (versus FAIL/PARTIAL/OPEN/BLOCKED) specifically for the rejection-semantics dimension, on the reasoning that since canon defines no rejection type or failure vocabulary at all, this dimension cannot be evaluated as a claim at all (there is nothing to test), which is categorically different from a dimension that was tested and found wanting.

rows.anchor: This mandate arrived after the work was done — so I checked it against the record instead of re-running it ... Re-executing this mandate would duplicate roughly 2.5 million tokens of completed work, so I did what the programme's duplicate-instruction discipline requires: verified against the record, reported, and did not blindly re-execute. Recorded as GN-87.
rows.statement: GN-87 records a 'duplicate-instruction discipline': when a detailed commissioning mandate arrives after equivalent work has already been completed (here, an estimated 2.5 million tokens of derivation and falsification work), the correct response is to verify the mandate's requirements against the completed record and report gaps rather than blindly re-executing the entire mandate from scratch. Three genuine gaps between the mandate and the completed work are identified and reported honestly, with one explicitly attributed as the commissioner's own fault: the reviewer mandate said 're-run its scripts yourself' rather than 'reconstruct the tests independently', so the completed review performed replication (copy, re-run, byte-identical confirmation, line-by-line code verification) rather than independent reconstruction -- real evidence, but weaker than the mandate required.
missing: independently written test code
the six Sigma/Q_t counterexample constructions
a semantic-isomorphism/distinctness test for the six registries

rows.anchor: P-11 is effectively the boundary between: 'we have explored possible operation algebras' and 'we have defined the candidate universe against which KnowledgeOS operations are allowed to be judged.' That makes it a foundational theory/architecture decision, not an administrative cleanup.
rows.statement: A correction is recorded against the characterization 'P-11 is cheap to state': while stating P-11 (what is the operation universe and what act closes it) may be linguistically cheap, resolving it is not cheap in consequence -- it is the foundational boundary between 'we have explored possible operation algebras' (exploratory) and 'we have defined the candidate universe against which KnowledgeOS operations are allowed to be judged' (a binding architectural decision), not an administrative cleanup task.

rows.anchor: For every proposition, identify whether it is: RATIFIED Explicitly adopted by an authority act. AUTHORIZED Allowed/binding within the governed architecture but not necessarily ratified as theory. FORMAL/DERIVED Mathematically or computationally established but not authoritative. PROPOSED/OPEN Candidate reasoning requiring a decision. Do not promote one layer into another.
rows.statement: Step 284's mandate fixes a four-layer epistemic classification discipline for every proposition in the programme: RATIFIED (explicitly adopted by an authority act), AUTHORIZED (binding within the governed architecture but not ratified as theory), FORMAL/DERIVED (mathematically or computationally established but not authoritative), and PROPOSED/OPEN (candidate reasoning requiring a decision) -- with an explicit prohibition on promoting a proposition from one layer to another without the appropriate act. A dependency graph is specified for the canonical operation registry with four branches (operation universe/P-11; mandatory capabilities/invariants+state model+evidence model+governance constraints; Reject semantics/P-1; authority boundary/A6+Article 8.3), each dependency to be classified CLOSED/OPEN/BLOCKING/NON-BLOCKING/UNRATIFIED, with an explicit warning not to mark anything 'closed' merely because an artifact discusses the issue.

rows.anchor: | Layer | Fundamental question | Current status | | Derivation | Why does this construct exist? | Partially established | | Definition | What exactly is this construct? | Partially canonicalized | | Architecture | How does it behave and compose in a system? | Partially established |
rows.statement: A tripartite (extended to six-part) gap taxonomy is proposed and declared must-not-be-merged: Derivation (why does this construct exist -- partially established), Definition (what exactly is this construct -- partially canonicalized), Architecture (how does it behave/compose in a system -- partially established), Implementation (how do we build it -- blocked in key areas), Governance (who makes it canonical -- partially established), Empirical (does the real system implement/observe it -- incomplete). This is offered as more useful than collapsing everything into a single undifferentiated 'theory gap' metric, and is accompanied by a deeper observation that some work jumped directly from 'derived idea' to 'candidate architecture' to 'implementation assumption' without passing through the intermediate stages of formal definition, semantic contract, and canonical architectural decision -- explaining a recurring corpus pattern of 'this was discussed' without ever reaching 'this was defined', 'this was derived', or 'this was ratified' (four distinct, frequently conflated epistemic states).

rows.anchor: The current evidence says roughly: 15 of 24 constructs have no real-environment observation. That cannot be solved by writing more theory. The real question is also whether the existing EKP actually exposes the constructs required to test the theory.
rows.statement: A five-gate roadmap to KnowledgeOS implementability is proposed: Gate 1 canonical theory boundary (Step 284's task: operation-universe provenance, Reject semantics, A6/Article 8.3 semantics, forward-only resolution semantics); Gate 2 canonical operation algebra (justified by canonical theory and required capabilities, then independently verified, then HPA-ratified -- explicitly not 'which list looks nicest'); Gate 3 transformation semantics (a formal delta: K x Operation -> K' with explicit pre/postconditions, invariant preservation, identity/equality, lineage, replay, evidence, authority, rejection semantics -- flagged as 'where the current work is still particularly weak'); Gate 4 implementation contract (V.1 through V.10 book chapters); Gate 5 real-system empirical validation, citing the existing finding that 15 of 24 KnowledgeOS constructs have no real-environment (EKP) observation, which cannot be solved by writing more theory, and questioning whether the existing EKP even exposes the constructs needed to test the theory at all.

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS theory is formally closed at the declared scope. But the canonical derivation chain, canonical definitions, and executable architectural semantics are not yet completely synchronized. ... | Derivation Gap | OPEN | ... | Definition Gap | OPEN | ... | Architecture Gap | OPEN |
rows.statement: The document's Final Verdict section asserts in the same breath that 'the KnowledgeOS theory is formally closed at the declared scope' and lists all three of its own named gap categories (Derivation, Definition, Architecture) as status OPEN with unresolved resolution steps required (Steps 285-288) -- an internal tension between claiming formal closure and simultaneously cataloguing open, unresolved architectural gaps as the document's own headline finding.

rows.anchor: δ: K × Operation × Policy × Authority → K' × Outcome Preconditions: - Valid(K) - Authorized(Operation, Policy, Authority) - Evidence(Operation) sufficient Postconditions: - Valid(K') - Invariant(K') = Invariant(K) - History(K') = History(K) ∪ {Event} - Identity preserved if Operation is refinement
rows.statement: A proposed general transformation-semantics signature delta: K x Operation x Policy x Authority -> K' x Outcome is sketched with preconditions (Valid(K), Authorized(Operation,Policy,Authority), sufficient Evidence(Operation)) and postconditions (Valid(K'), Invariant(K')=Invariant(K), History(K')=History(K) union {Event}, identity preserved if the operation is a refinement) plus invariants (Identity(K)=Identity(K'), Atma(K)=Atma(K'), and the non-attachment principle that EC=FALSE is an acceptable postcondition state) -- offered as the missing generic transformation contract shape, though none of Valid(), Invariant(), Authorized(), or sufficient Evidence() is itself formally defined here.

rows.anchor: REJECTED/CONFLICTED are reachable from any pre-boundary status by a governed act, never silently ... REJECTED does not occur in v0.2 at all (0 occurrences of 'reject' in v0.2 and v0.1) — it enters the Final Architecture only through D-FA-1 ... no-skip (I-12) governs the admission axis only
rows.statement: Precise primary-text findings sharpening earlier summaries: FA-1 §2's ratified text already types the act reaching REJECTED/CONFLICTED as governed and never silent (this is itself a ratified requirement, not merely an open question); REJECTED has zero occurrences in v0.2 or v0.1 and enters the Final Architecture only through D-FA-1 (sourced [E] to Constitution Arts. 7-9); and I-12's ratified scope, per FA-1 §2 itself, is explicitly limited to 'the admission axis only', with REJECTED and CONFLICTED placed off that axis -- meaning I-12 cannot be violated by a transition into or out of those states regardless of source status.

rows.anchor: Article 7 states no guard. Verbatim: REJECTED must be 'preserved as explicit epistemic states', 'never be knowledge', 'never silently discarded' ... No source status, no arity, no operation, no authority requirement. A repo-wide search for 'guard'/'precondition' across FA-1…FA-9, v0.2, the Constitution and RA v1.0 returns exactly one hit
rows.statement: A repo-wide search across FA-1 through FA-9, v0.2, the Constitution and Reference Architecture v1.0 for the terms 'guard'/'precondition' returns exactly one hit total, and it is unrelated (Constitution V.3, amendment discipline) -- confirming that Article 7 states requirements about REJECTED as a preserved epistemic state (never discarded, remaining part of the epistemic record) but specifies no source-status guard, arity, operation, or authority requirement of any kind for reaching it.

rows.anchor: Three mutually incompatible typings — R1 epistemic act on an item (→K', no authority; 256.11) · R2 governance transition, 'External', policy required (277 §277.3; 276 O_G ...) · R3 decision producer (Reject: Assessment × Authority × Policy → Decision; 250 §250.9, boxed UNRESOLVED) — plus one explicit refusal to type (249 §249.13: 'It may instead be … We do not know.' boxed OPEN).
rows.statement: Reject's typing across the corpus resolves to exactly three mutually incompatible readings that disagree on codomain and on whether authority is an input (R1: an epistemic act on an item with no authority, K x x x Reason -> K', from 256.11; R2: a governance transition classed External requiring policy, from 277/276, itself boxed 'not uniformly computationally demonstrated'; R3: a decision producer Assessment x Authority x Policy -> Decision, from 250 §250.9, boxed UNRESOLVED) plus one explicit refusal to type it at all (249 §249.13: 'We do not know', boxed OPEN). This is offered as a refinement of an earlier looser count of 'four rival readings' -- weaker as a count of actual specifications (since none of the three is an accepted specification) but stronger as evidence of genuine underdetermination.

rows.anchor: Y-2 · The conflict AF-F-31 alleges does not obtain. ... Operative classification: SEMANTIC UNDERDETERMINATION with a governance consequence — NOT a conflict between ratified propositions. ... Y-1 Any registry claiming to cover the ratified state model must contain at least one operation reaching REJECTED, and that act must be governed and never silent. This is derivable now, without P-1
rows.statement: AF-F-31's alleged conflict (that Reject's specification violates I-12 and Article 8) is determined NOT to actually obtain: it presupposes step 256.11 is a specification, but the primary text denies this explicitly and twice, and neither cited ratified constraint reaches (I-12 is scoped only to the admission axis, which REJECTED sits off; Article 8.1's governed-resolution requirement is already independently satisfied by FA-1 §2's own governed-act requirement). The operative reclassification is SEMANTIC UNDERDETERMINATION with a governance consequence, not a conflict between ratified propositions. Independently and positively, a governed-and-never-silent REJECTED-reaching operation is a derivable requirement on any registry covering the ratified state model RIGHT NOW, without resolving P-1 -- explaining why Reject appeared in the core of all six candidate registries without thereby licensing any of them. P-1's blocking scope is precisely bounded to claims that quantify over Reject's exact arity, codomain, source-status guard, or authority-typing (minimality, uniqueness, core-membership, invariant-compatibility claims), not the bare existence obligation.
missing: Reject's exact arity, codomain, and source-status guard (Z-1, Z-3)
whether reaching REJECTED from CONFLICTED counts as Art.8.1's 'governed resolution' or a distinct forbidden act (Z-4)

rationale_evidence.statement: G-01 (CRITICAL): 𝒪, the mandatory operation set, is never enumerated; ≡ is defined by ∀T∈𝒯 so the quantifier ranges over an open collection — ≡ is not undecidable, it is unconstructed. K*, A∈K, K1=K2, and the Step 259/266 sufficiency and minimality results all inherit this gap. Resolution requires HUMAN DECISION D-1, after which the gaps below it become derivable.

rationale_evidence.anchor:
The theory is not incomplete because it is missing answers. It is incomplete because it is
> missing a premise.
rationale_evidence.statement: Sharper statement of the theory's incompleteness: it is not missing answers, it is missing a premise — 𝒪, what KnowledgeOS is obliged to be able to do, was never written down, and five CRITICAL gaps are its shadow; a theory of sufficient state cannot be evaluated without the operations it must be sufficient for.

rationale_evidence.anchor:
> *"Zero is computable, total and terminating over finite R, **RELATIVE to per-requirement
> evaluators**.
rationale_evidence.statement: Computational closure is assessed CONDITIONALLY CLOSED: everything executed and computable (membership, equality, StructuralValid, contradiction detection, supersession, replay, lineage, Zero — 8/8 tests) is computable only relative to per-requirement evaluators (Γ semantics, HumanAuthorization oracles) that are themselves not established; the theory is computable down to its oracles, and the oracles are where the epistemics live.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Five of the five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes are the same object: Sigma. ... STEP 272 ... does not exist.
rationale_evidence.statement: All five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes (G-06 Sigma>=5 axes, G-25 Unknown homeless, G-27 Insufficient missing, G-11 evidence layer no inputs, G-12 no empirical relational structure) converge on the single object Sigma, matching the corpus's own Step 271 s271.35 marking Sigma RED and s271.36 commissioning the non-existent Step 272 to derive it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: |lower bound (forced)| = 14        |upper bound (named ∪ forced)| = 18 ... NOT derivable: which of the 4 band members are mandatory -- NORMATIVE -> D-1
rationale_evidence.statement: O is bounded but not determined: a 14-element lower bound and an 18-element upper bound are both derivable with no human input, along with the five-class partition and congruence rule (independently re-derivable since congruence is a property of an algebra's operations on its carrier, so an operation reading H is not an operation on K); only membership of the 4-operation undetermined band in the mandatory set is not derivable, because 'mandatory' is a normative predicate that no corpus of descriptions can entail -- this is D-1.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 'Determine' / determination object absent | this pass | G5 | Determination != Decision stated 19x -- the operation is forced and unenumerated ... 'Q' epistemic sufficiency dropped | independent | G5 | typed at 42.40, absent from the ratified 6-tuple
rationale_evidence.statement: Reconciled gap register across all three tracks classifies most findings as G5 (promotion): the Determine operation/object, D_t, the R 8-tuple, the ten-status set, Q epistemic sufficiency, (W,Omega)/Identifiable, U(H) uncertainty carrier, and 𝒦=(K,H) are all corpus-present constructions the canonical model never incorporated.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The largest class is G5 -- PROMOTION. Eight of thirty-four gaps are constructions the corpus already contains and the canonical model never incorporated. Two of them are running, passing code.
rationale_evidence.statement: Headline finding: of 34 reconciled gaps, G5 (promotion) is the largest class at 8, versus G1 (genuine semantic gap) at only 5 (of which just 3 are irreducible: Qualify's body, AuthorityAct's type, U's algebra) and G10 (normative) at 4 -- everything else is promotion, repair, vocabulary or a normative choice.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The theory's deficit was never discovery. It was transcription: three successive reductions (ℛ 8→3 fields, status 10→2 values, DC 7→6 components) each discarded something the corpus had established, and each loss was later rediscovered as a fundamental gap.
rationale_evidence.statement: Final headline argument answering the mandate's central question: KnowledgeOS does NOT need a new theory -- of 34 reconciled gaps, 8 are promotions (two running/passing code), 6 are repairs of execution-falsified formulations, 5 are refinements, 4 are normative choices, exactly 1 requires innovation; the recurring failure pattern is three successive transcription reductions (relation 8-to-3 fields, status 10-to-2 values, a 7-to-6-component DC reduction), each of which discarded corpus-established content that was later independently rediscovered as a 'fundamental' gap.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Chain verdict: links 1-3 are canonically supported (partially); links 4 and 5 are severed; links 6-7 are partial; links 8-9 have no canonical content at all; link 10 is specified but unrun.
rationale_evidence.statement: A ten-link canonical implementation chain is built (Canonical Objects, Canonical State, Canonical Invariants, Canonical Operations, Canonical Transformations, Evidence, Authority/Governance, Persistence, Replay, Tests), each classified PARTIAL/BLOCKED/OPEN with governed-only provenance. Links 4 (Operations) and 5 (Transformations) are severed/blocked; 8 (Persistence) and 9 (Replay) have no canonical content; 10 (Tests) is specified (EG-05) but unexercised.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Therefore the minimum canonical contract is: Operation registry (membership + criterion + closure claim) └─ per operation: Precondition Postcondition Invariant-preservation obligations ... plus: State identity + equality rule
rationale_evidence.statement: The mandate's proposed seven-field operation-contract shape (Operation+Precondition+Postcondition+Invariant preservation+Evidence effect+Authority effect+Replay effect) is necessary but not sufficient; three further components are canon-forced: (i) a closed operation registry with a membership criterion, (ii) typed rejection/failure semantics, (iii) a state identity and equality rule -- because postconditions are undecidable without state equality and per-operation contracts are incomplete without a closure claim.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Ratify a closed operation registry with a membership criterion -- or explicitly rule that none exists yet and mark the implementation contract BLOCKED at that point.
rationale_evidence.statement: The single smallest decision that would unlock implementation is ratifying (or explicitly refusing) a closed operation registry with a membership criterion; this single act unblocks links 4 and 5 of the chain and, through them, pre/postconditions, invariant-preservation obligations, and replay effects. No broad gap-discovery pass is indicated because the gap is undecided (a governance act is missing), not under-analysed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: THE TWO NAMED UNRECONCILED OPERATIONS (commission T-3) ... Split ... LinkEvidence
rationale_evidence.statement: The two operations the commission's T-3 task names as unreconciled against the executed algebra are Split and LinkEvidence; the script reports which sources name each.

rationale_evidence.anchor: RECOMMENDED: D — THE OPERATION UNIVERSE DEPENDS ON AN UNRESOLVED PRIOR CANONICAL DECISION ... the test did not fail and did not merely run out of evidence: it succeeded, produced a well-defined family of six minimal registries, and in doing so identified precisely which prior decisions determine membership
rationale_evidence.statement: The document recommends terminal verdict D over the weaker B (six registries exist, computed) or C (none is fit for ratification) -- D holds that the operation universe's membership depends on unresolved prior canonical decisions (P-1..P-10), which is offered as the most informative and actionable framing since the test succeeded (did not fail, did not run out of evidence) and precisely identified which decisions gate membership, led by the typing of Reject.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Every bound in the method biases toward fewer registries and more necessary operations — that is, toward verdict A. A result that nevertheless finds multiplicity is therefore reported against the bias of its own method.
rationale_evidence.statement: Every declared modelling commitment (M1-M6, six constructed operations, depth/witness-size/budget bounds) is analysed for which direction it biases the conclusion, and every one biases toward fewer registries and more necessary operations (toward a false single-answer verdict A). Since the test nonetheless found genuine multiplicity (six registries, a nine-operation undetermined band) despite every bound working against finding multiplicity, the multiplicity result is reported as robust to its own method's bias -- strengthening confidence that it is not a search artefact.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 23 operation blocks covering 24 operations ... 253 commission cells ... RATIFIED-SOURCED 27 ... EXECUTED 24 ... PROPOSED 12 ... NORMATIVE DECISION REQUIRED 69 ... no operation has a complete canonical contract, and none can have one until P-8/P-9/P-10 of MINIMALITY-RESULT.md §5.3 are settled.
rationale_evidence.statement: A mechanically-verified contract-completion scorecard over 23 blocks (276 rows, 253 commission cells, no blank cells): 27 cells RATIFIED-SOURCED, 24 EXECUTED, 12 PROPOSED, 69 marked NORMATIVE-DECISION-REQUIRED (46 of which are the two universally-open fields, invariant obligations and failure semantics; the rest are operation-specific). Compared against the governed baseline (OPERATION-CONTRACT-GAP.md §B: 2 cells fully fixed, 9 partial, 88 empty across 9 capabilities), this represents substantial new grounding, but the honest overall verdict stated is that no operation has a complete canonical contract, and none can until three named prior canonical decisions (P-8 state equality, P-9 closed invariant register, P-10 typed rejection vocabulary) are settled.
