rows.anchor: A. Birth-point table — five kinds, separated (Sat, Sat_c, EvalReq, Eval, Eval_c, Det_r, 𝒮, V_Sat, 𝒮_sat, 𝕊_sat, 𝒱, Status) ... Status ... NEVER DEFINED
rows.statement: Builds a five-column birth-point table (lexical/conceptual/first explicit definition/first mathematical type/first operational use) for twelve objects, finding an operational-use census (.py/.txt/.json, firewall excluded) of Det_r=0, EvalReq=0, V_Sat=0, S_sat=0, but Sat_c=17 -- flagging Sat_c as uniquely operationalized -- and flagging 'Status' (EvalRequirement's named codomain) as never defined anywhere, foreshadowing section E.

rows.anchor: B. ⭐⭐⭐ The finding that reverses my own: Sat_c was IMPLEMENTED AND RUN ... research/knowledgeos-sim/ ... The class-indexed branch was specified, implemented, adversarially tested and run in three phases. The contract-indexed branch has ZERO executable presence. ... My G-24 claim ... is TOO STRONG and is corrected.
rows.statement: Discovers research/knowledgeos-sim/ contains a full implementation campaign for Sat_c: a runner (run_satc.py), four modules (satc_spec.py, phaseC.py, repairs.py, zerolens.py), and result files spanning phase A spec, phase B adversarial testing, phase C zero-lens analysis, and additional evaluation/contradiction-pair results; zerolens.py explicitly documents 'the coarse projection pi: B->{T,F,U} -- what Sat_c did' (past tense, suggesting Sat_c was itself later superseded inside the simulation, not chased further here). Concludes the class-indexed (Sat_c) branch was specified, implemented, adversarially tested and run in three phases, while the contract-indexed (Det_r) branch has zero executable presence anywhere. Corrects the prior G-24 claim ('V_Sat has zero downstream consumers') as too strong: the SYMBOL V_Sat occurs in one document, but Sat_c the FUNCTION (whose codomain V_Sat is) has a full implementation and test campaign.

rows.anchor: C. Definition/version registry — every material formulation preserved ... No version deleted, none selected.
rows.statement: Records that every material formulation change (two new Sat rows, two new EvalReq rows, EvalContract, Eval, S_sat) is preserved in a definition-evolution-registry TSV, with no version deleted and none selected as canonical.

rows.anchor: D. Result-space identity matrix ... V_Sat × 𝒮_sat DISTINCT OBJECT — and INCOMPARABLE: V_Sat separates ⊥ (provably not satisfied) from U (undetermined). 𝒮_sat's single U = 'unsatisfied/unknown' MERGES exactly those two. ... The U test was the decisive instrument
rows.statement: Builds a result-space identity matrix over four codomains (S 9->10->11 elements never re-declared, 0 consumers; V_Sat 3 elements {top,bot,U} with U meaning 'cannot currently be determined', 17 executable consumers via Sat_c; S_sat 4 elements {S,U,P,C} with U conflating 'unsatisfied/unknown', 3 document consumers; S_sat notational variant used identically). Key finding: V_Sat x S_sat are DISTINCT AND INCOMPARABLE, not merely unmapped -- V_Sat separates bot (provably not satisfied) from U (undetermined) while S_sat's single U merges exactly those two meanings, and conversely S_sat has P (partial) and C (conflicted) that V_Sat lacks; neither refines the other and no projection or order is stated anywhere. S_sat x S_sat (notation variant) are SAME OBJECT with strong continuity; S x V_Sat, S x S_sat, S x S_sat(variant) are all IDENTITY UNWITNESSED. Calls the 'what does U mean' test the decisive instrument for distinguishing same-glyph-different-semantics cases.

rows.anchor: E. First, a correction to my own claim of two hours ago ... Checked at source: Status appears exactly ONCE in 025e — at L1008, as a bare arrow target. It is NEVER DEFINED. ... One section, two arrows: one codomain enumerated, the other only NAMED.
rows.statement: Retracts the immediately preceding document's claim that EvalRequirement's conceptual birth 'has the codomain' EvalReq lacks: checked at source, 'Status' appears exactly once in 025e (L1008) as a bare arrow target and is never defined -- 025e never mentions 'S', '025d', 'status set' or any enumeration. By contrast its sibling in the same section, EvalContract(K,EC,C)->ContractStatus, IS fully enumerated ({Ready,Blocked,Invalid,Indeterminate}). Concludes: in one section, two arrows -- one codomain enumerated, the other only named.

rows.anchor: The three-way classification §4 requires (PROVEN / TYPE-CONSTRAINED / INFERRED-and-withdrawn / IDENTITY UNWITNESSED) ... My earlier 'gap CLOSED' for EvalReq's codomain is DOWNGRADED to QUALIFIED.
rows.statement: Applies a mandatory three-way epistemic classification: EvalRequirement's codomain being NAMED 'Status' is PROVEN (boxed at 025e L1008); WHAT Status actually is remains NOT ESTABLISHED, not even inferred, with no cross-reference to 025d's S; EvalReq's codomain being V is TYPE-CONSTRAINED (forced by Det_r's domain applied to EvalReq's output, though the corpus never states this explicitly); the claim Status=V is INFERRED and explicitly WITHDRAWN here (nowhere established, different documents/lanes, 10 days apart, zero citation); EvalRequirement being identical to EvalReq is IDENTITY UNWITNESSED (same role/abbreviation but arity 3->4, C split into EC+Gamma, zero citation of EvalRequirement in theory-part-06). Concludes a codomain is named at birth and constrained by composition ten days later, but never actually defined, and the two arrows are not established to be the same function -- downgrading the earlier 'gap CLOSED' verdict for EvalReq's codomain to QUALIFIED.

rows.anchor: F. ⭐⭐⭐ The 2026-09-06 verdict — NOT a re-founding ... 23 documents, 00:23:01 → 07:51:53, ≈60,000 lines ... 025 appears zero times in all 23 documents. ... But the four citations in part-01 refute my reading
rows.statement: Measures the 2026-09-06 rewrite precisely: 23 documents, 00:23:01-07:51:53, approximately 60,000 lines, with 4 backward citations found only in part-01 and 0 in all 22 other parts (the string '025' appears zero times across all 23 documents). But the four citations in part-01 refute a simple 'discarded the past' reading: they state an epistemic policy about warrant ('I will not treat an attractive formulation as a theorem merely because it appeared in an earlier document'), DECLARE CONTINUITY ('the existing corpus gives us a strong starting point... the corpus explicitly rejected the earlier unique minimal kernel claim'), and twice EXERCISE INHERITANCE by citing corpus-adopted or corpus-withdrawn results as binding authority ('the corpus explicitly adopted history-preserving delta', 'the corpus explicitly withdrew the previous unique-minimality claim').

rows.anchor: §7's mandated distinction, resolved: policy to re-derive ≠ semantic decision to replace. It is the first, not the second. ... Inherit what the corpus has explicitly ADOPTED or explicitly WITHDRAWN. Re-derive everything that merely appeared.
rows.statement: Resolves the mandated policy-vs-replacement distinction: the 2026-09-06 rewrite is a POLICY TO RE-DERIVE, not a semantic decision to replace -- it nowhere declares prior Sat/EvalRequirement/S formulations wrong or superseded; its actual rule is 'inherit what the corpus has explicitly ADOPTED or explicitly WITHDRAWN [via governance act]; re-derive everything that merely appeared.' Concludes the near-zero citation count (0 of 22 parts) is the MEASURED EFFECT of this policy rather than evidence of a declared restart, because almost nothing in the 025-series ever received an explicit governance act (independently corroborated by the earlier G-00 finding that no governance act touches most of this material).

rows.anchor: ⛔ Withdrawal: 'Re-founding #6 — and the first witnessed one' WITHDRAWN. Re-founding #1 (031) drops the 025 apparatus; this document calls the corpus 'a strong starting point' and inherits from it twice. correct classification: DECLARED SELECTIVE-INHERITANCE REWRITE ... This is a better finding than the one it replaces: the corpus is not being discarded. It is being filtered through a rule that almost nothing passes.
rows.statement: Formally withdraws the immediately preceding document's classification of the 2026-09-06 event as 're-founding #6, the first witnessed one', contrasting it with the genuine re-founding #1 (031, which explicitly drops the 025 apparatus) -- this document instead calls the corpus 'a strong starting point' and inherits from it twice. Adopts the corrected classification DECLARED SELECTIVE-INHERITANCE REWRITE: continuity declared, inheritance keyed to governance status, re-derivation everywhere else. Explicitly frames this correction as strictly better than what it replaces: the corpus is not being discarded, it is being filtered through a rule that almost nothing passes.

rows.anchor: G. Gap impact — §9 dependency test, one claim withdrawn ... G-25 → C-1 UNWITNESSED — WITHDRAWN ... Different subscript, different index, different object from Loss_{ℛ_req}. And it is the set rendering — C-1's non-scalar branch
rows.statement: Re-tests G-25's claimed downstream dependencies: G-25->Det_r is DIRECT (Det_r is born inside theory-part-06 SS6.18); G-25->G-01 is DIRECT (2 of Sat's 4 codomains, S_sat and S_sat-variant, are born inside the rewrite); G-25->G-05 is DIRECT BUT THIN (theory-part-02 L1437 gives a one-line R_req(Q,Gamma) subset-of Dist(R(K)) form the verification lane never independently writes); G-25->C-1 is UNWITNESSED and WITHDRAWN (the rewrite's Loss_T, in parts 08/12/18, is a transformation loss with a SET adequacy condition Loss_T intersect Dist_EC(K)=empty -- a different subscript, different index, different object from Loss_R_req, and notably itself the SET rendering that is C-1's non-scalar branch). Revises G-01 (unchanged as re-scoped, but now two of six codomain pairs are PROVEN distinct rather than merely unmapped) and G-24 (corrected: the gap is not 'no consumers' but 'the implemented branch was not carried forward').

rows.anchor: H. TheoryState impact — which historical states change ... None. Every correction here is to my reconstruction, not to any TheoryState(t) ... No later evidence was back-propagated.
rows.statement: Confirms strict TheoryState(t) discipline: none of the historical states themselves change -- every correction in this document is to the RECONSTRUCTION's own prior claims, never to a TheoryState(t) at a past moment. Table maps each corrected claim (t=08-27 'has the codomain'->'names one'; t=09-02 'zero consumers'->'17 executable'; t=09-06 're-founding #6'->'selective inheritance') to its original historical state. Confirms no later evidence (e.g. Sat_c's implementation) was back-propagated to claim an earlier document (025e) knew of it.

rows.anchor: I. Remaining unresolved, after this reconstruction: What is Status? ... Why was the implemented branch not carried forward? ... V_Sat × 𝒮_sat incomparability ... EvalRequirement ≟ EvalReq ... Det_r's body FIREWALL-LIMITED — not MISSING
rows.statement: Lists five genuinely remaining unresolved questions after this reconstruction: (1) what Status actually is -- the only codomain in the family with no elements at all defined anywhere; (2) why the implemented Sat_c branch was not carried forward while Det_r (which has none) became the theory-part-06 formulation -- framed as the measured cost of the selective-inheritance policy; (3) the V_Sat x S_sat incomparability, unreconcilable without an explicit decision that does not exist; (4) whether EvalRequirement equals EvalReq, IDENTITY UNWITNESSED; (5) Det_r's body, correctly classified FIREWALL-LIMITED (97% of occurrences firewalled) rather than MISSING. Confirms nothing canonicalized, no definition selected, no result space merged, firewall honoured throughout.

rows.anchor: ⛔ Determination is not born at 155a ... Our previous architecture identified Determination. I would now make its semantics explicit. ⇒ RECONSTRUCTION ONLY / retrospective import ... Compare Det_r ... Strong structural similarity, zero citation ⇒ IDENTITY UNWITNESSED.
rows.statement: Corrects Determination's apparent 155a birth: the source itself says 'our previous architecture identified Determination; I would now make its semantics explicit', classifying this as RECONSTRUCTION ONLY / retrospective import, not a true concept birth -- the corpus-wide earliest occurrence is actually in reviews/ (2026-08-19 00:57), a governance lane, nine days earlier. Records 155a's formalization Determination=f(Claim,Evidence,Method,Context) with f unnamed and no codomain, plus Evidence!=Determination and Verification subset-of Determination. Compares this to Det_r:VxEC->S_sat (born 09-06): 155a carries the 'how' as an explicit Method argument while Det_r carries it as a function-name index plus EC -- strong structural similarity but zero citation between them, classified IDENTITY UNWITNESSED.

rows.anchor: ⛔ WITHDRAWAL — the 'five re-foundings' record ... G-25 already removed the sixth. This reconstruction removes the concept. ... apparatus is lost across declared continuities. Authors say they continue, and mean it; the objects do not travel with the declaration.
rows.statement: Formally withdraws the corpus's own '07-THEORYSTATE-CHRONICLE.md' record of five re-foundings (031, 183-pre, 230, 262, 273), revising each label: 031's 'INDEPENDENT_REFOUNDING (drops the 025 apparatus)' is corrected -- 031 itself says it continues Steps 1-30; it is actually 026 that drops the apparatus while declaring continuity, the opposite framing; 183-pre's 'EXPLICIT_REPLACEMENT (pruning)' is downgraded to SELECTIVE_REJECTION since it affirms alignment and rejects only a named subset; 230's 'UNWITNESSED' becomes REDUCTION since it explicitly presupposes the existing architecture; 262's 'EXPLICIT_REPLACEMENT' becomes CORRECTION since it names its predecessor and corrects one specific conclusion; 273 unchanged. Concludes (with G-25 having already removed the sixth candidate) this reconstruction removes the whole 're-founding' CONCEPT itself, replacing five separate events with one general mechanism: in this corpus, apparatus is lost across declared continuities -- authors say they continue and mean it, but the objects do not travel with the declaration.

rows.anchor: The codomain defect is inherited across three eras ... Status ... Determination = f(Claim,Evidence,Method,Context) ... none ... EvalReq(K,r,EC,Γ) ... none ... Three objects, three eras, three lanes — the same defect, never noticed by any of them.
rows.statement: Identifies a single recurring defect across three unrelated objects, eras and lanes: Status (025e, 08-27) is named but never defined; Determination=f(Claim,Evidence,Method,Context) (155a, 08-28) has no codomain at all; EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma) (theory-part-06, 09-06) has no codomain (V is only type-constrained, never stated). Concludes this identical defect recurs across three separate objects, eras and lanes, never noticed by any of them independently -- generalizing the earlier per-object findings into a single corpus-wide pattern.

rows.anchor: §1–4 · The 025→026 boundary, object by object — and my G-12 headline qualified ... The concepts did not stop. They de-formalised. ... sufficiency 73% ... satisfaction 45% ... contract 40% ... The NOTATION was lost. The CONCEPTS ran on through 45–73% of the interval.
rows.statement: Qualifies the prior G-12 finding that the 025 apparatus 'vanishes' at step 026: while all formal 025 SYMBOLS score exactly 0 across 265 files (confirmed true), a census of the underlying 025-era CONCEPTS in prose form finds sufficiency at 73% (193/265 files), satisfaction at 45% (120/265), contract at 40% (107/265), gap at 20%, acceptance criterion at 2%, while the specific phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0. Concludes the NOTATION was lost but the CONCEPTS ran on informally through 45-73% of the interval -- the earlier headline ('the apparatus vanishes') is true only of formal notation, not of underlying concepts.

rows.anchor: And precisely which form survived ... Of 241 satisf* occurrences sampled: 83 in technical context, 158 prose. ... What survived is satisfaction as a PREDICATE. What was lost is satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.
rows.statement: Samples 241 'satisf*' occurrences (83 technical, 158 prose) and verifies at ten specific steps (s070,079,081,086,091,092,095,097,098,101) that the surviving technical usage is uniformly an unformalised predicate ('the rule is satisfied', 'invariants remain satisfied') rather than the 025-series typed function Satisfied(K,r,EC) with three typed arguments and a result space S(9->10->11). Concludes precisely what survived was satisfaction AS A PREDICATE; what was lost was satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.

rows.anchor: An interpretation, marked as such ... consistent with — and would explain — the four divergent Sat codomains found in G-25 ... nothing carried a result space through the interval, so each later lane supplied its own. ⛔ Recorded as [PROPOSED], not as a cause.
rows.statement: Proposes, explicitly marked as an unproven interpretation (not a corpus-stated cause), that the loss of a shared result space during the interval would explain why G-25 later found four mutually non-citing Sat codomains (S 9-11, V_Sat 3, S_sat 4, S_sat variant): each later lane, lacking an inherited result space, supplied its own. Notes this hypothesis is recorded as [PROPOSED] rather than established, citing a cautionary precedent -- a previously withdrawn batch-003 claim ('the semantics-bearing argument always disappears') that failed for exactly the same overreach.

rows.anchor: §6 · Distributed completeness — the corrected classification ... EvalReq is the only 025-era object whose concept as well as its notation leaves the interval. That singles it out, and it is the one object G-25 found still untyped at 09-06.
rows.statement: Provides a corrected four-row classification: '025 apparatus vanishes at 026' is corrected from PARTIALLY-EVIDENCED to DE-FORMALISED (symbols 0, concepts 45-73%); 'Sat is absent from 026-268' stands for the FUNCTION but is FALSE for the underlying CONCEPT (0 vs 120 files); 'EvalReq is absent' stands fully, both notation and concept (even the phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0/265); 'Omega-B has no type' is REFUTED (excluded by design, per S14). Concludes EvalReq is uniquely the only 025-era object whose CONCEPT, not merely its notation, actually leaves the interval -- and it is the same object G-25 separately found still untyped as late as 09-06.

rows.anchor: §8, §12 · Identity and DDD — EC is the interval's worst case ... Three ECs, three arities, three bounded contexts, zero cross-references ... Verdict: HOMONYM ×3, IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair.
rows.statement: Identifies EC as a triple homonym with zero cross-references between any pair: EC=EpistemicClaim (s032, 11-tuple, 'the atomic unit of KnowledgeOS'); EC=engineering change (s117, 8-tuple, 'a test object' in a traceability experiment); EC=EpistemicContract (025-series, (R_G,Gamma_G) shape, 0 occurrences in steps 026-154). Classifies this as HOMONYM x3 with IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair, noting it is the same shape of finding as Determination (governance vs mathematical vs Det_r) and Gamma (four senses), already recorded elsewhere in this programme.

rows.anchor: §7 · Mathematical typing across the interval (PROVEN: Ω-2, K_v0, K_v1, EC-claim, Γ_A, EC-engchange; UNKNOWN: Zero never defined, Δ_t only α_t defined, Ω_t unresolved, Update 10 signatures) ... No promotion of TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED to PROVEN.
rows.statement: Audits mathematical typing status across the interval: PROVEN objects include Omega-2 (W->O), K_v0 (9-tuple, s028), K_v1 (7-tuple, s031), EC-claim (11-tuple, s032), Gamma_A (4-tuple, s053), EC-engchange (8-tuple, s117); UNKNOWN status objects include Zero (never defined anywhere in 265 files), Delta_t (one occurrence, whose 'where' clause defines only a sub-component alpha_t, not Delta_t itself), Omega_t as an argument of delta_K (signature declared unresolved by its own cited sources), and Update (10 unrelated signatures). Notes no TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED-status object was promoted to PROVEN in this pass.

rows.anchor: §11 · Senior-statistician audit ('satisfaction continues' 120 files/many independent lineages; '025 symbols absent' 0 hits × 265 files/1 measurement; Ω-B 'philosophical anchor' 33 files/1 lineage)
rows.statement: Applies the programme's senior-statistician discipline (distinguishing occurrence counts from independent evidential lineages) to its own three headline claims: 'satisfaction continues' (120 files) is genuinely MANY independent lineages spread across s070-s101+ and multiple sub-lanes; '025 symbols are absent' (0 hits x 265 files) is only ONE measurement, not 265 confirmations; Omega-B's 'philosophical anchor' framing (33 files) is only ONE lineage, a single continuous Gita/Lord-Lens thread from 08-26 onward.

rows.anchor: §15 · Classification of what this pass touched (Ω-B upgraded B; satisfaction-concept B / satisfaction-function C; EvalReq D genuine corpus gap for the interval, exhausted search; EC E; Zero/Δ_t E)
rows.statement: Issues final classifications for this pass: Omega-B is upgraded from D to class B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES -- defined semantically at birth, its absent type being a declared exclusion, not a gap); the satisfaction CONCEPT is class B (continues as a predicate across the interval) while the satisfaction FUNCTION remains class C (competing definitions, per G-25); EvalReq is class D (GENUINE CORPUS GAP for the interval specifically, on an now-exhausted search -- both notation and concept score 0 in all 265 files); EC is class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, three homonyms); Zero and Delta_t are class E (used throughout but never defined within the interval).

rows.anchor: §10 · Negative-history discipline ... Coverage qualifier preserved: ≈1.5% of the readable corpus is read semantically. No corpus-wide negative claim is made from this slice — the EvalReq finding is scoped to the interval, and Ω-B's is scoped to its own 33-file history.
rows.statement: States the negative-history search scope precisely (265 files of 026-268 plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for Omega-B's type across its 33-file history and for the 025 concepts) and preserves an explicit coverage qualifier: only approximately 1.5% (32 of 2,099 files) of the readable corpus has been read semantically by this whole gap-discovery programme so far. Explicitly refuses to generalize any finding beyond its search scope -- the EvalReq absence is scoped to this interval only, and Omega-B's exclusion-by-design finding is scoped to its own 33-file history only. Confirms firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no definition selected or merged.

rows.anchor: First, the admission. I classified EvalReq as D — GENUINE CORPUS GAP on ONE PHRASE SEARCH ('requirement evaluation' = 0/265). §15 forbids exactly that, and it is the fourth time this pass has caught the same error in my own work.
rows.statement: Opens with a self-admission: the EvalReq='D-GENUINE CORPUS GAP' classification (from S2918/G-12-semantic) rested on a single phrase search ('requirement evaluation', 0/265), which the programme's own methodology explicitly forbids as sufficient grounds for a gap claim -- noted as the fourth time in this investigation pass that the same single-search error has been caught in the investigator's own prior work.

rows.anchor: §1, §8 · The widened search — my single phrase was hiding two live objects ... requirement + satisf* 15 ... Eval( / Evaluate( as a function 9 ... Notation absent — concept present. The zero was real for eight variants and wrong for two.
rows.statement: Runs eleven search variants for requirement-evaluation across the 265-file 026-268 interval: nine variants correctly score 0 (EvalReq/EvalRequirement, the phrase 'requirement evaluation', 'evaluate/evaluating a requirement', requirement+evaluat* co-occurrence, requirement status/check*/met/fulfil*, contract-specific evaluation), but two variants that the prior single-phrase search missed score positive: 'requirement + satisf*' (15 hits) and 'Eval(/Evaluate(' as a function (9 hits). Concludes the notation was genuinely absent for eight variants but the concept was present via two variants the earlier search missed.

rows.anchor: §2, §9 · The genuine birth point is neither EvalReq nor EvalRequirement ... DV-23 ... Eval(P,K) ∈ {T,F,U} with the §25 connective tables (step-018) ... The evaluation family is born at STEP-018 — before the 026–268 interval AND before the 025-series.
rows.statement: Finds (via verification/DEFINITION-VERIFICATION-REGISTER.md's DV-23 entry, citing step-018) that the true birth point of the entire evaluation family is Eval(P,K) in {T,F,U} with connective tables at step-018 -- earlier than both the 026-268 interval and the entire 025-series. Discloses step-018 itself falls in the 001-022 band, an acknowledged backfill debt for this reconstruction lane, so its content here is taken secondhand from the verification lane's citing register, not yet read at primary source.

rows.anchor: §3, §7 · The chronology — and it splits into TWO families (8-event table, step-018 through theory-part-06) ... The corpus typed, verified and carried PROPOSITION-evaluation for ten days — and never once gave REQUIREMENT-evaluation a result space.
rows.statement: Traces eight chronological evaluation events (step-018 Eval(P,K); 025d's Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) via a colliding oplus operator; 025e's EvalRequirement(K,r,C)->Status named-never-defined; a four-document {T,F,U} carry-through 08-29/08-30; s240's independently exhaustively checked strong-Kleene verification with commutativity/associativity/monotonicity proven; s241's necessary-not-sufficient dependency hypothesis sigma=Eval(...); Sat_c's V_Sat={top,bot,U}; theory-part-06's uncodomained EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma)) and splits them into two families: PROPOSITION-evaluation (Eval(P,K), Eval(P,E,K,C,pi,...)) with a verified, continuous {T,F,U} codomain and algebraic laws, versus REQUIREMENT-evaluation (Evaluate, EvalRequirement, EvalReq, Sat_c) with an oplus-structured/undefined-Status/none/V_Sat set of incompatible, non-algebraically-verified codomains and no independent computation except Sat_c's later implementation. Concludes the corpus typed, verified and carried proposition-evaluation continuously for ten days while never once giving requirement-evaluation a result space.

rows.anchor: §5 · Identity — EvalRequirement ≟ EvalReq, and both ≟ Eval ... Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) × EvalRequirement(K,r,C) SAME CONCEPT — REFINED ... Eval(P,K) × the requirement family RELATED OBJECT — DIFFERENT SUBJECT ... Eval(P,K)'s {T,F,U} × Sat_c's V_Sat={⊤,⊥,U} SAME OBJECT — STRONG CONTINUITY
rows.statement: Runs four identity tests: EvalRequirement x EvalReq remains IDENTITY UNWITNESSED (unchanged from G-25); Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) x EvalRequirement(K,r,C) is SAME CONCEPT-REFINED (written two minutes apart, 025d 18:31:42 to 025e 18:33:20, same subject, the contract argument retained as EC_G->C); Eval(P,K) versus the whole requirement-evaluation family is RELATED-DIFFERENT-SUBJECT (P is a proposition, r is a requirement -- evaluating a claim is not evaluating a requirement, and no document identifies them); Eval(P,K)'s {T,F,U} and Sat_c's V_Sat={top,bot,U} are SAME OBJECT-STRONG CONTINUITY (same three values, same 'undetermined' third value, an unbroken chain 08-29->08-30->09-02, though with no citation between the endpoints -- continuity is measured, not declared).

rows.anchor: §4 · Distributed completion — what this changes for G-25 ... V_Sat = {⊤,⊥,U} is NOT invented at 09-02. It descends from Eval(P,K) ∈ {T,F,U}, born step-018, Kleene-verified at s240. ⇒ Classification for the three-valued space: B — COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES
rows.statement: Revises G-25's finding of four unreconciled Sat codomains: shows V_Sat={top,bot,U} is NOT an independent 09-02 invention but descends directly from Eval(P,K) in {T,F,U}, born step-018 and algebraically Kleene-verified at s240 -- reclassifying the three-valued space as B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES: step-018 supplies connective tables, s240 supplies algebraic verification, Sat_c supplies requirement-class indexing and a body). Notes the 4-valued S_sat and the 9->11 S remain unreconciled with it -- G-25's incomparability result for those two stands untouched.

rows.anchor: §6 · Mathematical typing ... Eval(P,K) → {T,F,U} PROVEN ... that space is strong Kleene, comm./assoc./monotone PROVEN ... V_Sat ≡ {T,F,U} TYPE-CONSTRAINED — no document states the identity ... any codomain for EvalRequirement/EvalReq UNKNOWN, at every point in 10 days
rows.statement: Typing audit: Eval(P,K)->{T,F,U} is PROVEN with connective tables stated; the space being strong Kleene with commutativity/associativity/monotonicity is PROVEN via s240's independent exhaustive check; V_Sat being identical to {T,F,U} is only TYPE-CONSTRAINED (same three values and semantics, but no document ever states the identity explicitly); EvalReq->V remains TYPE-CONSTRAINED (unchanged from G-25); Status=V remains INFERRED and withdrawn; any codomain at all for EvalRequirement/EvalReq is UNKNOWN at every single point across the ten-day history. No TYPE-CONSTRAINED claim was promoted to PROVEN in this pass.

rows.anchor: §7 · The Req → EvalReq → Sat → Determination chain ... The chain is not established end-to-end. Two of six edges are UNWITNESSED/POSSIBLE, and the corpus never draws it as one pipeline.
rows.statement: Tests a six-edge candidate pipeline Req->EvalReq->Sat->Determination for direct evidential support: Req->Evaluate(K_t,r,EC_G) is DIRECT (025d SS25D.37, r in R_G); Evaluate->EvalRequirement is DIRECT (2-minute gap, same subject); EvalRequirement->EvalReq is UNWITNESSED (10 days, zero citation); EvalReq->Sat is DIRECT (theory-part-06 SS6.18 explicitly composes them); Sat->Determination is only POSSIBLE (Det_r is INSIDE Sat's definition, not downstream of it, and Determination's own birth is in a governance lane, 08-19); Eval(P,K)->Sat_c is only POSSIBLE (the codomain plausibly descends but with no citation). Concludes the full chain is not established end-to-end -- two of six edges are unwitnessed or merely possible, and the corpus never draws the whole thing as one pipeline anywhere.

rows.anchor: §12 · Provenance ... {T,F,U} is the evaluation codomain: ≥3 independent lineages ... requirement-evaluation is never typed: 1 measurement over 265 files + 4 named formulations — not 4 confirmations

rows.statement: Issues final terminal classifications: proposition-evaluation Eval(P,K) = class A (COMPLETE HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION -- birth, evolution, algebraic verification and terminal descendant V_Sat all located); the three-valued space = class B (COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES); requirement-evaluation = class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, corrected from the earlier D -- four formulations, three shared subjects, zero cross-citations, and no result space at any point). rows.statement: Records gap-register impact: EvalReq's D (GENUINE CORPUS GAP) classification is WITHDRAWN and replaced with E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED); G-25 is RE-SCOPED since V_Sat now has a traced ancestry, reducing the unreconciled codomain count from four to three; G-01 is RE-SCOPED since the three-valued space is shown to be the OLDEST member of the evaluation family, not a late narrowing; Det_r remains unchanged, FIREWALL-LIMITED; a NEW gap G-27 is opened naming the asymmetry itself as the finding -- requirement-evaluation has been named four times across ten days and given a result space zero times, while its sibling proposition-evaluation was typed at birth and algebraically verified.

rows.anchor: §15 · Negative-history ... Result: NOTATION ABSENT · CONCEPT CONTINUES · DEFINED IN MULTIPLE STAGES — not GENUINE CORPUS GAP. step-018 is NOT YET READ (backfill debt)
rows.statement: Confirms the exhaustive negative-history search (265 interval files x 11 variant patterns, both spellings, plus the whole non-firewalled corpus for {T,F,U} and Evaluate(...) argument shapes) yields the correct classification NOTATION ABSENT / CONCEPT CONTINUES / DEFINED IN MULTIPLE STAGES, not GENUINE CORPUS GAP. rows.statement: Lists four concrete historical-search tasks that must be resolved from the corpus rather than decided mathematically: (A) whether the corpus actually defines Accept or an equivalent under another name, with a specific search-term lineage list (accept, acceptance, acceptance condition, sufficient, sufficiency, qualification, qualify, threshold, established, establishment, independent support, support criterion, admissibility, evidence standard); (B) whether Gamma is actually authority, a responsible actor, a responsibility relation, an acceptance owner, a governance constraint, or something else; (C) whether Eval, Eval_c, Standing and Det_r are the same function, a refinement, a specialization, genuinely different functions, or merely analogous terminology; (D) whether the satisfaction codomain is historically {0,1} or {top,bot,U}, explicitly refusing to choose mathematically and deferring to whichever the corpus's historical lineage actually decides.

rationale_evidence.anchor: And precisely which form survived ... Of 241 satisf* occurrences sampled: 83 in technical context, 158 prose. ... What survived is satisfaction as a PREDICATE. What was lost is satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.
rationale_evidence.statement: Samples 241 'satisf*' occurrences (83 technical, 158 prose) and verifies at ten specific steps (s070,079,081,086,091,092,095,097,098,101) that the surviving technical usage is uniformly an unformalised predicate ('the rule is satisfied', 'invariants remain satisfied') rather than the 025-series typed function Satisfied(K,r,EC) with three typed arguments and a result space S(9->10->11). sources.note: The Engineering Decision Model (the catalog of engineer decisions, e.g. DeterminePlacement); its adoption is tested as uneven.

rows.anchor: Q1 — what problem was the model created to solve? ... "this model says what decisions an Engineer resolves with them"
rows.statement: The Engineering Decision Model was created because standards say what the rules are, while the model says what decisions an engineer resolves with them: rules existed but the decisions they answer were unindexed. Its anti-problem: it is a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook (ARB, 2026-07-11) — created to prevent duplicated authority, not to add a layer. Its birth act included a vocabulary correction (2026-07-11): a DDD Domain Service is executable, a decision is a specification. Its adoption bar: one real engineering cycle must show consistent resolution through the model; it is DRAFT until earned.

lineage_claims.quote: a DDD Domain Service is executable; a decision is a specification

rows.anchor: Q2 — which decisions does it explicitly model? ... Eight — all of one family
rows.statement: Eight decisions are explicitly modeled, all of one family (the flow of knowledge and artifacts through governed work), grouped by question: 'Where does it belong?' (DetermineConcern, DeterminePlacement - mechanized by doc-placement.php); 'What is it/does it live?' (DetermineArtifactLifecycle - deletion litmus, DetermineArtifactType); 'Is it worth keeping/raising?' (DetermineReusePotential - Harvest, DeterminePromotionPath - ladder entry); 'What governs/verifies it?' (DetermineApplicableStandards, DetermineQualificationMethod). Deliberately excluded: ADR-making, capability approval, authority acts, promotion rulings — 'promotion is a human governance act and is never automated'; 'the AI evaluates and recommends — authority remains with governance.' The absence of governance decisions from the catalog is design, not gap.

rows.anchor: Q3 — which discovered decisions are not represented? ... FREEZE and RETIRE extend nothing in the catalog
rows.statement: Answered in a prior Discovery pass and carried forward unchanged: FREEZE (n>=3, undeclared authority) and RETIRE (PM-6) extend nothing in the catalog, submitted as insufficiency evidence per the model's own stopping rule. Implicit but exercised: the challenge-commissioning trigger and terminology adoption. Nothing further found in this pass, which per the stopping rule is the correct amount.

rows.anchor: Q4 — does it govern the full ladder, or only architecture decisions? ... NEITHER — and the answer is the INVERSE of the commission's suspicion
rows.statement: The model governs zero architecture decisions (no DetermineArchitectureDecision exists; ADRs are governance acts, outside the catalog by design). What it governs on the ladder Observation->Hypothesis->Evidence->Principle->Architecture is the entry points, not the rungs: DetermineReusePotential opens the ladder (observation->candidate); DeterminePromotionPath routes onto it (candidate->pilot->qualification->ARB decides). The rungs belong to ES-006.1, and the model correctly refuses to own them since it is an index, never a second rulebook.

rows.anchor: Q5 — Knowledge Governance or only Engineering Governance? ... Engineering Governance NOW; Knowledge Governance ANTICIPATED
rows.statement: The model's own Decision Catalogs table states Engineering Standards answer the catalog's Engineering Decisions, while Project-Knowledge-class Knowledge Decisions (DetermineKnowledgeNeed, Source, Representation, Qualification, Promotion) are 'pilot-gated candidates — arrive only with pilot evidence; same pattern, different domain.' Engineering Governance is present now; Knowledge Governance is anticipated with the arrival condition already stated, and the entire ontology/meta-model corpus of this programme is exactly the kind of pilot evidence the anticipated catalog says it is waiting for.

rows.anchor: Q6 — extend the model, or map onto it? ... MAP. Tested element by element
rows.statement: Ontology/meta-model elements map onto the existing decision model rather than extending it: archetype classification extends DetermineArtifactType (same question, richer vocabulary); KNOWLEDGE != ARTIFACT (I-1) is presupposed by DetermineArtifactLifecycle's deletion litmus; AUTHORITY-SCOPE/CONTAINER boundary maps to DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS/EVIDENCE-STATUS maps to DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE (normative force) maps to DetermineApplicableStandards. Nothing in the ontology requires a new decision; the only extension pressure (FREEZE/RETIRE) is not ontology-driven, but comes from the enacted governance record. Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

rows.anchor: Q7 — would a second decision model violate ubiquitous language? ... YES — three times over
rows.statement: A second decision model would violate ubiquitous language three times over: (1) the model's charter states it is 'a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook' — a v2 is exactly what it exists to prevent; (2) I-5, lint-enforced, requires one authoritative artifact per topic+context, so a second model is a literal violation; (3) ES-005.4 requires one rule -> one home. A competing 'KnowledgeOS Decision Model' would have been the UL violation and was not created; the Discovery and Validation passes are readings of the one model, not rivals to it.

rows.anchor: U-EDV-1 | Does the DA intend the anticipated PKS-class Knowledge Decision catalog (§5) to be the home of the knowledge-governance decisions this programme surfaced?
rows.statement: U-EDV-1: does the Decision Authority intend the anticipated PKS-class Knowledge Decision catalog to be the home of the knowledge-governance decisions this programme surfaced — waits on the ARB, natural companion to D-8.

rows.anchor: U-EDV-2 | The model's adoption test (one real cycle of conscious use) — unevenly met (U-DM-4, carried)
rows.statement: U-EDV-2: the model's adoption test (one real cycle of conscious use) is unevenly met (U-DM-4, carried forward), waiting on EP-02 of the next real cycle.

rows.anchor: DP-n as a distinct layer between principle and capability ... UNIQUE HYPOTHESIS — needs operational proof
rows.statement: DP-n as a distinct architectural layer between principle and capability has no direct external counterpart found (policy-as-code practice is only adjacent); it remains a unique hypothesis requiring operational proof.
missing: operational proof

rows.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
rows.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

rows.anchor: RESULT: THE MODEL DOES NOT SURVIVE INTACT. One claim FALSIFIED · two WEAKENED · two SURVIVED · two unchanged
rows.statement: Overall falsification result: of the domain model's claims, one is falsified, two weakened, two survived, two unchanged; the strongest claim in the model (D-2) was among those weakened, by evidence the model itself had cited. Method: every test executed against artifacts, not reasoned from the model, using the repository's own instruments (Round47-OP's nine admissible justifications, the R16 Workbook Strong/Medium/Weak scale); four falsifiers were sought, three landed.

rows.anchor: W-1 · D-2's "own decision series" is a shared authority — two of four grounds fall
rows.statement: D-2's claim of 'its own decision series, ADR-M distinct from ADR-AIP' is weakened: Round39-D6's header states decision authority for all ADRs is 'sponsor + ARB' and amendment requires sponsor+ARB approval, so ADR-M is a scoping device under a shared authority, not a separate authority. Its claim of 'independent evolution' is falsified: Round39-D6 states the ADRs 'were authored together on 2026-06-25' — a series written in one sitting evidences independent subject, never independent evolution over time. This matches the ARB Chair's named falsifier 'ADR separation is historical rather than semantic' — half true: separation is real in subject, absent in time.

lineage_claims.target: D-2's 'own decision series, independent evolution' claim
lineage_claims.quote: FALSIFIED as evolution. Round39-D6: 'Retrospectively documented. These ADRs were authored together on 2026-06-25.'

rows.anchor: S-1 · D-2 survives on a ground I had not weighted — an explicit mutual scope exclusion
rows.statement: D-2 survives on a new ground: Round39-D6's verbatim rule 'Governance discoveries (constitutional/capability) MUST NOT appear here. No DDD concepts here' is a deliberately maintained boundary (not an accident of filing), bidirectional in effect (ADR-M excludes governance, ADR-AIP carries no methodology rules), and survives the shared-authority finding since a shared authority that forbids itself from mixing two subjects is evidence FOR two models, not against. D-2 remains a boundary, but on subject exclusion, not on decision-series separation or independent evolution.

rows.anchor: S-3 · D-1 survives every falsifier
rows.statement: D-1 survives every falsifier sought: no multiple owners of the same concept found (DA/ARB throughout), no changes that fail to co-occur (ES set moves under STANDARDS_INDEX), no forced co-evolution with a product (ratification and freeze are product-independent), no absent invariants (append-only rulings, R-46).

rows.anchor: U-1 | Was Round39-MC adopted by sponsor authority BECAUSE D-2 is independent, or DESPITE it being part of D-1?
rows.statement: U-1: was Round39-MC adopted because D-2 is independent, or despite it being part of D-1 — the artifacts record the act but never the reason; only the sponsor and ARB know, and the model's validity turns on it.

rows.anchor: U-4 | Is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced, or was it stated once?
rows.statement: U-4: is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced or was it stated once — stated 2026-06-25, no subsequent enforcement event found.

rows.anchor: U-6 | Does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers?
rows.statement: U-6: does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers — carried forward, now sharper: shared ARB suggests peers-under-one-authority, not hierarchy.

rows.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
rows.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

rows.anchor: Recommendation — per domain ... The model as a whole | REVISE, then re-test ... NOT canonical
rows.statement: Per-domain recommendations: D-1 ACCEPT; D-2 REVISE (restate the boundary on the one surviving ground, Round39-D6's scope exclusion; delete 'own decision series' and 'independent evolution' as grounds); D-3 DEFER (untestable at n=1, revisit when a second runtime adapter exists); D-6a DEFER, D-6b ACCEPT; D-5 ACCEPT the demotion (do not promote until ARB overturns H-CAT-1 on evidence); D-4 ACCEPT the rejection; D-7 REVISE (restate as an observation of one instance, record PKS-as-projection as falsified). Overall the model as a whole: REVISE then re-test, NOT canonical — 2 of 8 accept, 3 revise, 2 defer, 1 accept-as-rejection.

rows.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
rows.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q1 — what problem was the model created to solve? ... "this model says what decisions an Engineer resolves with them"
rationale_evidence.statement: The Engineering Decision Model was created because standards say what the rules are, while the model says what decisions an engineer resolves with them: rules existed but the decisions they answer were unindexed. Its anti-problem: it is a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook (ARB, 2026-07-11) — created to prevent duplicated authority, not to add a layer. Its birth act included a vocabulary correction (2026-07-11): a DDD Domain Service is executable, a decision is a specification. Its adoption bar: one real engineering cycle must show consistent resolution through the model; it is DRAFT until earned.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q2 — which decisions does it explicitly model? ... Eight — all of one family
rationale_evidence.statement: Eight decisions are explicitly modeled, all of one family (the flow of knowledge and artifacts through governed work), grouped by question: 'Where does it belong?' (DetermineConcern, DeterminePlacement - mechanized by doc-placement.php); 'What is it/does it live?' (DetermineArtifactLifecycle - deletion litmus, DetermineArtifactType); 'Is it worth keeping/raising?' (DetermineReusePotential - Harvest, DeterminePromotionPath - ladder entry); 'What governs/verifies it?' (DetermineApplicableStandards, DetermineQualificationMethod). Deliberately excluded: ADR-making, capability approval, authority acts, promotion rulings — 'promotion is a human governance act and is never automated'; 'the AI evaluates and recommends — authority remains with governance.' The absence of governance decisions from the catalog is design, not gap.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q3 — which discovered decisions are not represented? ... FREEZE and RETIRE extend nothing in the catalog
rationale_evidence.statement: Answered in a prior Discovery pass and carried forward unchanged: FREEZE (n>=3, undeclared authority) and RETIRE (PM-6) extend nothing in the catalog, submitted as insufficiency evidence per the model's own stopping rule. Implicit but exercised: the challenge-commissioning trigger and terminology adoption. Nothing further found in this pass, which per the stopping rule is the correct amount.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q4 — does it govern the full ladder, or only architecture decisions? ... NEITHER — and the answer is the INVERSE of the commission's suspicion
rationale_evidence.statement: The model governs zero architecture decisions (no DetermineArchitectureDecision exists; ADRs are governance acts, outside the catalog by design). What it governs on the ladder Observation->Hypothesis->Evidence->Principle->Architecture is the entry points, not the rungs: DetermineReusePotential opens the ladder (observation->candidate); DeterminePromotionPath routes onto it (candidate->pilot->qualification->ARB decides). The rungs belong to ES-006.1, and the model correctly refuses to own them since it is an index, never a second rulebook.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q5 — Knowledge Governance or only Engineering Governance? ... Engineering Governance NOW; Knowledge Governance ANTICIPATED
rationale_evidence.statement: The model's own Decision Catalogs table states Engineering Standards answer the catalog's Engineering Decisions, while Project-Knowledge-class Knowledge Decisions (DetermineKnowledgeNeed, Source, Representation, Qualification, Promotion) are 'pilot-gated candidates — arrive only with pilot evidence; same pattern, different domain.' Engineering Governance is present now; Knowledge Governance is anticipated with the arrival condition already stated, and the entire ontology/meta-model corpus of this programme is exactly the kind of pilot evidence the anticipated catalog says it is waiting for.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q6 — extend the model, or map onto it? ... MAP. Tested element by element
rationale_evidence.statement: Ontology/meta-model elements map onto the existing decision model rather than extending it: archetype classification extends DetermineArtifactType (same question, richer vocabulary); KNOWLEDGE != ARTIFACT (I-1) is presupposed by DetermineArtifactLifecycle's deletion litmus; AUTHORITY-SCOPE/CONTAINER boundary maps to DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS/EVIDENCE-STATUS maps to DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE (normative force) maps to DetermineApplicableStandards. Nothing in the ontology requires a new decision; the only extension pressure (FREEZE/RETIRE) is not ontology-driven, but comes from the enacted governance record. Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q7 — would a second decision model violate ubiquitous language? ... YES — three times over
rationale_evidence.statement: A second decision model would violate ubiquitous language three times over: (1) the model's charter states it is 'a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook' — a v2 is exactly what it exists to prevent; (2) I-5, lint-enforced, requires one authoritative artifact per topic+context, so a second model is a literal violation; (3) ES-005.4 requires one rule -> one home. A competing 'KnowledgeOS Decision Model' would have been the UL violation and was not created; the Discovery and Validation passes are readings of the one model, not rivals to it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: S-1 · D-2 survives on a ground I had not weighted — an explicit mutual scope exclusion
rationale_evidence.statement: D-2 survives on a new ground: Round39-D6's verbatim rule 'Governance discoveries (constitutional/capability) MUST NOT appear here. No DDD concepts here' is a deliberately maintained boundary (not an accident of filing), bidirectional in effect (ADR-M excludes governance, ADR-AIP carries no methodology rules), and survives the shared-authority finding since a shared authority that forbids itself from mixing two subjects is evidence FOR two models, not against. D-2 remains a boundary, but on subject exclusion, not on decision-series separation or independent evolution.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
rationale_evidence.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

rationale_evidence.anchor: FINDING 1: the platform has a decision CATALOG for engineers and only a decision LOG for governance
rationale_evidence.statement: Engineer decisions (resolved by applying a governed procedure) are indexed as a catalog (the eight decisions of the Decision Model); governance decisions (resolved by an authority act, by DA/ARB/sponsor) are recorded richly (R-1..R-77 rulings, DR-1..DR-8, the ADR series, the Decision Docket D-1..D-9b) but cataloged nowhere. Whether that asymmetry is a defect or the correct shape is recorded as U-DM-1, not resolved.

rationale_evidence.anchor: FINDING 2: exactly TWO recurring decisions extend nothing in the existing set — FREEZE and RETIRE — and both already carry the operational evidence the stopping rule demands
rationale_evidence.statement: Every recurring decision found in the enacted record was tested against the stopping rule's own question ('which existing decision does this extend?'). All but two map onto existing catalog entries. FREEZE/UNFREEZE extends nothing found, exercised n>=3 (methodology freeze 2026-08-01, architecture freeze 2026-08-03, corpus freeze Phase A), each time by declaration under no named authority, procedure, or reversal condition. RETIRE/PRESERVE knowledge extends nothing (PM-6 asks exactly this, still open); retirement meanwhile happens informally by supersession. Both are submitted as insufficiency evidence for the Decision Model's own ladder, not as new catalog entries, which only the ARB may mint.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q4 — which ontology elements exist BECAUSE they support a decision ... KNOWLEDGE ≠ ARTIFACT (I-1) | DetermineArtifactLifecycle | the deletion litmus … is UNASKABLE unless knowledge and its file are different things
rationale_evidence.statement: Nine ontology elements are each bound to the specific decision they serve, applying Evans' test: KNOWLEDGE!=ARTIFACT (I-1) underwrites the deletion litmus of DetermineArtifactLifecycle (unaskable unless knowledge and file differ); AUTHORITY-SCOPE serves DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS serves DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE:normative-force serves DetermineApplicableStandards; DP-n anchoring serves the approve-capability-change decision; CONTAINER boundary would serve the extraction/adoption decision (the MVK FAIL is this decision made without the model); PROJECTION+attestation (corrected I-4) serves the trust-or-rebuild decision; EVIDENCE-STATUS serves the earns/grants promotion gate; the four partial orders serve the direction-of-change-propagation decision.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The chain — tested, not assumed ... DESIGN POLICY (DP-n) ... ADMIT — DISCOVERED. Neither of us named it ... ENGINEERING DOMAIN owns Capability ... REJECT as an owner
rationale_evidence.statement: Testing the reviewer's proposed chain Mission->Strategy->Principles->Capability: ENGINEERING STRATEGY is admitted (12+ charter artifacts); ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE is admitted (six registers with own identifier series: AIP-01..14, AP-1..10, PGP-01..05, MC-01..08, SD-1..7, DR-1..8); DESIGN POLICY (DP-n) is discovered as a new anchor, since the Capability Catalog binds every capability to a DP (CAP-001->DP-1, etc.) and neither the reviewer nor the author had named it; 'Engineering Domain owns Capability' is rejected — no artifact links any CAP-n to a PD-n; the reviewer's concern that capabilities must not float is correct, but the repository already anchors them to DP-n, not to a domain. Chain: MISSION -> STRATEGY -> PRINCIPLE -> DESIGN POLICY -> CAPABILITY -> KNOWLEDGE -> ARTIFACT.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Out-of-Boundary Register — 14 reaches, 3 of them contamination ... REACH #13 IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THE EXPERIMENT ... The record is more favourable to the MVK than reality warrants
rationale_evidence.statement: 14 out-of-boundary reaches recorded, of which 3 are contamination (2 recognized and refused: doc-placement.php + the 14-phase Operating Loop; 1 disclosed: the bootstrap sequence itself, supplied by the experiment brief rather than the MVK). Reach #13 is flagged as the most important line: left to the MVK alone, the session would have begun at 'Idea -> Implementation Plan' without modeling a context first — the record is therefore more favorable to the MVK than reality warrants, and the true state is worse than FAIL suggests.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The three load-bearing failures ... F-1 The EEP cannot be satisfied at bootstrap ... F-2 There is no genesis path ... F-3 REFUTED 2026-08-02. RESTATED: the method EXISTS but is product-coupled
rationale_evidence.statement: Three structural failures: F-1 the EEP cannot be satisfied at bootstrap (forbids one party holding both Engineer and Independent Reviewer, forbids skipping stages, forbids implementing before approval, and the light gate EP-01-Light is the source project's property — the MVK forbids proceeding and supplies no lawful way to proceed); F-2 there is no genesis path (the sole sanctioned route to an architecture requires operational evidence absent on day one and explicitly forbids idea->ADR->implementation); F-3, originally 'there is no strategic-DDD method', is refuted and restated: the method exists (Round47-00 Strategic DDD Constitution, Round47-OP Operating Protocol, with nine product-neutral boundary criteria and a rejection protocol) but is product-coupled via SD-1, which admits only PublicDigit's Certified Domain Knowledge Release — the bootstrap session could not see them because they were not included in the MVK file list.
